Oṃ, salutation to the Supreme Goddess.
The Kāmadhenu Tantra.
The First Chapter.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
O God of gods, O Mahādeva, you who are proficient in all the Āgamas!
Now, O Lord of the Gods, [I shall speak of] the supreme fifty-syllable [mantra].
O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, tell me the nature of reality;
out of grace, O Īśāna, tell it to me if I am dear to you.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
Now I shall fully declare this secret that is most strictly concealed, by the mere knowledge of which a man becomes liberated while living (jīvanmukta). 1.3.
O Goddess, if one should mutter the Great Vidyā without knowing the principles of mantra, all of that is in vain; what is the use of his recitations and worship? (1.4)
If there is no knowledge of the phonemes through the concentration of meditation and likewise through the samādhi of yoga, what is the use of his recitation and worship? (1.5)
The wondrous seed-syllable consisting of fifty letters resides in my throat;
it is pure, endowed with various colors, and the supreme essence of all tantras. (1.6)
The Goddess who is the fifty Mātṛkās, eternally consisting of various vidyās;
likewise, the Goddess who consists of various vidyās and who consists of the Great Vidyā (Mahāvidyā). 1.7.
The Goddess who consists of all castes, who consists of all gods, the supreme;
the gentle one who consists of all gods, the supreme mother of the cosmic egg. 1.8.
Having bowed down many times with devotion, I shall speak; listen, O beloved!
The Mātṛkā, beginning with the letter 'a' and ending with the letter 'kṣa', is the embodiment of the seed-syllables (bīja). 1/9.
The Visarga and the Bindu are the embodiment of Brahmā consisting of the three powers;
from the phoneme (Varṇa) Brahmā is born, and likewise Viṣṇu is produced.
And Rudra is born, O Goddess, the agent of the world's dissolution;
she who resides in my throat is Śāradā, the fair-eyed one.
O lotus-faced goddess, I am Śiva, having held within my throat the various seeds situated in her womb. (1.12)
Listen, O fair-faced one, to the truth of the letter *A*, which is most secret:
it is ever like the autumnal moon and consists of five sheaths. (1.13)
The color consists of the five deities and is endowed with the three powers;
though devoid of qualities, it is possessed of the three qualities, being itself the embodiment of absolute liberation.
She herself, whose form is primordial nature (prakṛti), consists of the phoneme composed of the principle of the bindu.
Thus ends the first chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The second chapter.
The venerable Mahādeva said: O beloved, its form is most wonderful, consisting of the light of a conch shell.
O beloved, [I am] the color consisting of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, as well as Rudra himself.
The syllable consisting of the five vital breaths is herself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī;
she is the letter *i*, the supreme bliss, with the luster of a fragrant flower. (2.2)
O beloved, the complexion consists eternally of Hari and Brahmā, and is always joined with Rudra;
O Goddess, it is likewise eternally composed of Śakti, as well as the Guru, Brahmā, and the Self.
The phoneme consisting of Sadāśiva is endowed with the Supreme Brahman;
the phoneme consisting of Hari and Brahmā is endowed with the three qualities (guṇas). || 2.4 ||
O Supreme Goddess, the letter *i* is indeed the form of Kuṇḍalinī herself;
O Supreme Goddess, the letter *ī* is herself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (2.5)
The complexion consists eternally of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, as well as Rudra;
it is composed of the five deities and has the form of a streak of yellow lightning.
O Supreme Goddess, the syllable *U* consists eternally of the four gnoses and the five vital breaths; it is the Savior (*Tāra*) and is Kuṇḍalinī herself. (2.7)
Resembling a yellow campaka flower, it is eternally composed of the five deities and the five vital breaths, O Goddess, and bestows the four aims of human existence.
O Goddess of the gods, the syllable *A* is a seed-mantra most difficult to obtain;
its form is like a conch or a jasmine flower, and it is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (2.9)
The phoneme always consists of the five vital breaths and the five deities;
likewise, the phoneme is endowed with the five vital breaths and is composed of the three qualities. (2.10)
The syllable joined with three dots (bindus), like a streak of yellow lightning, bestows dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, and always grants happiness. (2.11)
O Supreme Goddess, the syllable *ṛ* is Kuṇḍalī herself in embodied form;
here, O fair-faced one, are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra as well. (2.12)
The phoneme is ever united with Sadāśiva; it is always conjoined with Īśvara.
The phoneme consists of the five vital breaths (prāṇas) and is eternally composed of the four types of knowledge. (2.13)
I bow to the syllable *Ṛ*, which has the form of a red streak of lightning;
O Supreme Goddess, the syllable *Ṝ* is herself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (2.14)
Always having the form of a yellow streak of lightning, it consists of the five deities;
it is the color consisting of the four gnoses and always consists of the five vital breaths. (2.15)
O beloved, O lady with tremulous glances, I always bow to the syllable *ḷ*, which is endowed with the three powers; it is Kuṇḍalinī, the supreme deity. (2.16)
O beloved, here Brahmā and all the others always abide;
this complexion consists eternally of the five deities and the four types of knowledge. (2.17)
The phoneme endowed with five vital breaths (prāṇas), likewise consisting of the three qualities (guṇas), and composed of three points (bindus), is like a streak of yellow lightning. (2.18)
O Supreme Goddess, the letter *ḹ* has a luster equal to the full moon;
it is eternally the syllable consisting of the five deities and the five vital breaths. (2.19)
O Goddess, she who consists of the three qualities (guṇas), likewise consists of the three points (bindus); she bestows the four aims of life and is herself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī.
The letter E is supreme and divine, consisting of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva;
resembling the Bandhūka flower, it is eternally composed of the five deities. (2.21)
The phoneme consists of the five vital breaths and likewise consists of the three points (bindus);
O Goddess, it bestows the fourfold group of goals and is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (2.22)
Thus ends the second chapter in the venerable Kāmadhenu Tantra.
The third chapter:
The syllable *ai* is supremely divine; it is itself Mahākuṇḍalinī, resembling ten million moons and eternally composed of the five vital breaths.
O beloved, the phoneme consists of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, as well as Rudra;
it consists of Sadāśiva and is endowed with the three points (bindus).
O lady with tremulous eyes, [worship] the syllable *oṃ*, which always consists of the five deities,
which has the form of a red streak of lightning, and which is the Lord whose nature is the three qualities (*triguṇa*).
I bow to the Mother of the Gods, whose form consists of the five vital breaths;
O Maheśānī, this very form is herself the Supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (3.4)
The syllable *au*, appearing like a streak of red lightning, is Kuṇḍalā herself;
O beloved, Brahmā and all the others abide here eternally. (3.5)
The phoneme consisting of the five vital breaths is eternally composed of Sadāśiva;
it is always united with Īśvara and bestows the four aims of human existence. (3.6)
The syllable AṂ, conjoined with the Bindu, possessing a radiance like yellow lightning, is a phoneme consisting of the five vital breaths and embodying the deities beginning with Brahmā. (3.7)
The phoneme consisting of all-knowledge, endowed with the three points (bindus), is the phoneme consisting of the three powers; it is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (3.8)
O Supreme Goddess, the syllable *Aḥ* is always accompanied by the *visarga*;
O Supreme Goddess, the syllable *Aḥ* consists of the radiance of red lightning.
The phoneme is always composed of the five deities and composed of the five vital breaths;
the phoneme consists of all knowledge and is joined with the principles beginning with the Self (ātman). (3.10)
The phoneme consists eternally of the three drops and the three powers;
all [the goddesses] are youthful in age and devoted to song, instrumental music, and the like.
These young women are Śiva’s own Kuṇḍalinī in embodied form. (3.11)
Now I shall fully declare the supreme reality of Kāra, a secret most wonderful; listen to it from me, O you who belong to the three worlds. (3.12)
The left line is Brahmā, Viṣṇu is the right path;
the lower line is Rudra, and the Mātrā is Maheśvarī herself. (3.13)
Kuṇḍalī is shaped like a hook; Sadāśiva is the void in the center.
O fair-faced one, the left line resembles the hibiscus flower or liquid lac. (3.14)
The right line resembles the autumnal moon and is embodied;
the lower line, O lady of beautiful hips, has the luster of a great emerald. (3.15)
Her fame is like a conch shell or a jasmine flower; she is the mother Sarasvatī herself.
She who is Kuṇḍalī and Aṅkuśā has the form of ten million streaks of lightning. (3.16)
Resembling ten million moons, Sadāśiva is eternally empty in the center;
Kālī, who bestows the state of absolute liberation (kaivalya), resides within that void-womb. (3.17)
From the letter *ka* arises everything: desire, liberation itself, wealth, and likewise dharma, O Goddess; it is not otherwise. (3/18)
The letter *ka* is indeed the root-nature (*mūlaprakṛti*) of all phonemes;
it is the granter of desires, possessing the form of desire, throbbing and imperishable. (3.19)
O Maheśānī, she who is the passionate woman, naturally beautiful herself, is the mother of all the gods and the bestower of the state of absolute liberation. (3.20)
Kāmā, situated in the upper corner, is said to be the power of Brahmā;
Jyeṣṭhā, situated in the left corner, is said to be the power of Viṣṇu;
and the Bindu, situated in the right corner, is Raudrī, whose nature is withdrawal.
But for what purpose, O lady of beautiful limbs, is that [knowledge] fourfold in nature? (3.22)
The power of will (icchā-śakti) is Brahmā, Viṣṇu possesses the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti), Rudra is the power of action (kriyā-śakti), and all [this] has Prakṛti as its form. (3.23)
The seat of the Goddess Tripurā consists of the principles of Ātman, Vidyā, and Śiva, which are eternally essential and non-abiding; it is the letter *ka*, comprising the five deities. (3.24)
O Goddess of the gods, the Lord resides within that triangle;
this triangle is said to be the supreme Yoni-maṇḍala. (3.25)
She whose [soles] are merely the foreparts of the feet is proclaimed as Kāminī.
Om! [One should meditate upon] the supreme Kāminī, who resembles the vermilion in the bedchamber. (3.26)
She has four arms and three eyes, is adorned with creeper-like arms, and is embellished by two breasts shaped like kadamba buds. (3.27)
The Supreme Goddess was adorned with ornaments such as jeweled armlets and bracelets,
and graced by necklaces of gems and garlands of flowers.
Having thus understood the passionate woman, one should recite the syllable *ka* ten times;
then, having meditated upon her as being in full bloom, one shall partake in the fruit of the recitation.
This, O Goddess, is the supreme reality (*tattva*) of the syllable *ka* that has been told to you. (3/29)
Thus ends the third chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The Fourth Chapter.
The Illustrious Mahādeva said:
O Supreme Goddess, [the syllable] *ka* is conjoined with the three Kuṇḍalinīs.
The letter Kha is most wonderful, possessing a radiance like that of a conch shell or a jasmine flower.
O Goddess, it possesses three corners, is void, and is endowed with three points; it is joined with the three qualities and is eternally composed of the five deities.
I bow to the syllable *kha*, endowed with the three powers;
and to the syllable *ga*, O Supreme Goddess, which is eternally the essence of the five deities. (4.3)
O Dear One, [He is] devoid of qualities yet endowed with the three qualities, eternally effortless and stainless,
consisting of the five vital breaths, the primordial sound (varṇa), and the essence of all powers.
I bow to Kuṇḍalinī, who resembles the rising sun; O lady with tremulous glances, she is eternally the letter *gha* and the nature of the four-cornered [triangle]. 4/5.
The complexion consisting of the five deities is like the rising sun;
though devoid of qualities, it is endowed with the three qualities and is eternally united with the three qualities.
I bow to the letter Gha, which is all-pervading, all-bestowing, and peaceful;
O Supreme Goddess, the letter Ṅa is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī.
O lady with tremulous eyes, I bow to the syllable *ṅa*, which consists of all the letters, possesses the three qualities (*triguṇa*), and is composed of the five vital breaths (*pañcaprāṇa*). 4/8.
Listen to the letter *ca*, O lady of beautiful hips, which bestows the fourfold aims of human life;
joined with *Kuṇḍalī*, O Goddess, it is itself the supreme *Kuṇḍalī*. (4.9)
It is eternally joined with Kuṇḍalinī, always consisting of the five deities;
it is the syllable consisting of the five vital breaths, and is always of the nature of the five vital breaths. (4.10)
O Dear One, the syllable *cha*, endowed with the three powers and accompanied by the three dots, is most wonderful; it is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (4.11)
It is eternally endowed with the Kuṇḍalinī, always consisting of the five deities;
it is the syllable consisting of the five vital breaths, always accompanied by the three powers.
I bow to the syllable *cha*, which is endowed with three dots (the bindu), eternally joined with the Lord (*īśvara*), and has the form of a streak of yellow lightning. 4/13
O Supreme Goddess, the letter Ja itself is the central Kuṇḍalinī;
it resembles the autumn moon and is eternally endowed with the three qualities (guṇas). (4.14)
O Dear One, the phoneme always consists of the five deities and the five vital breaths;
it is accompanied by the three powers and endowed with the three points.
O Supreme Goddess, the syllable Jha is Kuṇḍalī, whose form is liberation;
she has the appearance of a red flash of lightning and is eternally established in the three qualities (guṇas). 4/16
The syllable is always composed of the five deities and consists of the nature of the five vital breaths;
the syllable is always accompanied by the three points (bindus) and accompanied by the three powers (śaktis).
O beautiful one, listen to the syllable *ña*, which is eternally united with the Lord;
it has the form of a streak of red lightning and is itself the supreme *Kuṇḍalinī*. (4.18)
The phoneme is always composed of the five deities and the five vital breaths;
the phoneme is always accompanied by the three powers and the three points (bindus). (4.19)
O lady of tremulous glances, the letter Ṭa is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī;
it has the form of ten million streaks of lightning and is eternally composed of the five deities.
The phoneme endowed with the five vital breaths, possessed of the three qualities, the phoneme accompanied by the three powers, and always joined with the three points. (4.21)
O lady with tremulous eyes, the letter *ṭha* is Kuṇḍalinī, whose form is liberation;
she has the appearance of a yellow streak of lightning and is eternally endowed with the three qualities (*guṇas*). (4.22)
The phoneme consists eternally of the five vital breaths and is composed of the five vital breaths;
the phoneme is accompanied by the three points and is always joined with the three powers. (4.23)

O lady with tremulous glances, the letter *ḍa* is always endowed with the three qualities (*triguṇa*), consists of the five deities, and is eternally composed of the five vital breaths (*pañcaprāṇa*). (4.24)
The syllable is always accompanied by the three powers and endowed with the three points;
it consists of the fourfold knowledge and is united with the principles beginning with the Self. (4.25)
I bow to the syllable *ḍa*, which has the form of a streak of yellow lightning;
and to the syllable *ḍha*, the supreme object of worship, who is herself the supreme Kuṇḍalī.

I bow to the syllable *ḍha*, which is eternally composed of the five deities and the five vital breaths; it is always conjoined with the three qualities (*guṇas*) and united with the principles (*tattvas*) beginning with the Self (*ātman*); it has the appearance of a streak of red lightning. (4.27)
O Supreme Goddess, the letter Ṇa is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī;
it has the form of a yellow streak of lightning and is eternally composed of the five deities. (4.28)
O Goddess, it consists of the five vital breaths, is always joined with the three qualities (guṇas), is united with the principles beginning with the Self (ātman), and bestows great delusion. (4.29)
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The Fifth Chapter. Śrī Mahādeva said:
O lady of tremulous glances, the letter *ta* is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī.
The phoneme consists of the nature of the five deities and likewise consists of the five vital breaths.
The syllable accompanied by the three powers, joined with the principles beginning with the Self, and the syllable endowed with the three points, possessing a radiance like yellow lightning. (5.2)
O lady with tremulous eyes, the letter *tha* is adorned with earrings and is the form of liberation;
it is always accompanied by the three powers and the three points (*bindu*).
I bow to the syllable *Tha*, which consists of the five deities, is eternally composed of the five vital breaths (*prāṇas*), and resembles the rising sun. 5/4.
Listen to the letter *da*, O lady of beautiful limbs, which bestows the four aims of life;
it is a syllable consisting of the five deities and is eternally composed of the five vital breaths. (5/5)
O Goddess, she who is always endowed with the three powers and accompanied by the three points, united with the principles beginning with the Self, is herself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (5.6)
Meditate on the syllable *da* in the heart, having the form of a red streak of lightning;
O Supreme Goddess, the syllable *dha* is Kuṇḍalinī, whose nature is liberation. (5.7)
It is eternally united with the principles beginning with the Self, consisting of the five deities,
and always composed of the five vital breaths, O Goddess, together with the three powers.
Meditate upon the syllable *Dha* in your heart, accompanied by three dots (*bindu*), appearing like a streak of yellow lightning and bestowing the four aims of human life. (5.9)
Listen to the letter *na*, O lady of beautiful limbs, which has the form of a red flash of lightning;
this syllable consists of the five deities and is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (5.10)
O Pārvatī, contemplate the syllable consisting of the five vital breaths within your heart;
hereafter, I shall explain the syllable *pa*, which bestows liberation. (5.11)
The phoneme that bestows the four aims of life, possessing a luster equal to the autumn moon, is composed of the five deities; it is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (5.12)

The phoneme consisting of the five vital breaths, always accompanied by the three powers, is a phoneme devoid of the three qualities (guṇas) and joined with the principles beginning with the Self (ātman). (5.13)
O Pārvatī, meditate upon the syllable that bestows great liberation within your heart;
O lady of beautiful limbs, hear the letter *pha*, which resembles a flash of red lightning. (5.14)
The syllable that bestows the fourfold aims of life always consists of the five deities;
the syllable always consists of the five vital breaths and is eternally united with the three qualities.

O lady of beautiful limbs, listen to the syllable *baka*, which is eternally joined with the reality of the Self and others, accompanied by the three points (*bindus*), and bestows the four aims of human existence. (5.16)
Always resembling the autumnal moon, consisting of the five deities, always composed of the five vital breaths, and eternally endowed with three dots (bindus), is the syllable. (5.17)
I perpetually bow down to that syllable which is endowed with the three powers, eternally fashioned from nectar, and which is itself the manifest Kuṇḍalinī. (5.18)
Listen to the letter *bha*, O lady of beautiful limbs;
it is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī, the syllable that bestows great liberation, resembling the color of the rising sun. (5.19)
The phoneme consists eternally of the five vital breaths and the five deities;
O Dear One, the phoneme is accompanied by the three powers and endowed with the three points (bindus).
Listen to the letter *ma*, O lady of beautiful limbs;
it is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī, resembling the rising sun and bestowing the four aims of human life. (5.21)
I perpetually bow to that syllable which is endowed with the three powers, accompanied by the three dots (bindus), united with the principles beginning with Ātman, and residing in the heart. 5/22.
Listen to the letter *ya*, O lady of beautiful limbs; it is always four-cornered, resembling the smoke of straw, and is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (5.23)
The phoneme is always composed of the five vital breaths and consists of the five deities;
likewise, the phoneme is accompanied by the three powers and endowed with the three points (bindus). || 5.24 ||
I always bow to the color, the embodied [form], and imperishable liberation.
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between Deva and Dvīpa.
The Sixth Chapter.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
O lady with tremulous glances, [the syllable] "Ra" is conjoined with two Kuṇḍalīs.
It always has the form of a red streak of lightning and consists of the nature of the five deities.
O Goddess, this syllable consists of the five vital breaths, is always accompanied by three dots (bindus),
joined with the three powers (śaktis), and conjoined with the principles beginning with the Self (ātman).
O lady with tremulous glances, I perpetually bow to the syllable *la*, which consists entirely of splendor and is joined by the three *kuṇḍalīs*. (6.3)
Having the form of a yellow streak of lightning, bestowing all jewels, consisting of the five deities, and always composed of the five vital breaths (prāṇas). 6/4.

Meditate always in your heart upon that syllable, which is endowed with the three powers, accompanied by the three points (bindus), and joined with the principles beginning with the Self (ātman). (6.5)
O lady with tremulous eyes, the syllable *va* is the eternal liberation of the Kuṇḍalinī;
it is the letter consisting of the five vital breaths, always accompanied by the three powers.
The syllable, accompanied by three dots (bindus), conjoined with the principles beginning with Ātman, consists of the five deities and resembles a streak of yellow lightning. (6.7)
O Goddess, this syllable, which consists of the four aims of life and bestows all accomplishments, is always accompanied by the three powers and is indeed ever united with the three powers. (6.8)
O Supreme Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, the letter Śa is golden-colored;
its radiance is red-hued, and it is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (6.9)
O Goddess, the letter Śa bestows the fourfold aims of life; it is the embodiment of Brahman, O Beloved, a syllable consisting of the five deities and composed of the five vital breaths.
The syllable is always joined with rajas, sattva, and tamas, accompanied by three dots (bindus),
endowed with the three powers (śaktis), and united with the principles beginning with the Self (ātman).
Listen to the letter *ṣa*, O lady of beautiful limbs; it always consists of six corners, resembles a red moon, and is itself the supreme Kuṇḍalinī. (6.12)
The syllable that bestows the fourfold aims of life, whose form is fashioned from nectar, which consists eternally of the five deities and the five vital breaths. (6.13)
O Pārvatī, meditate in your heart upon that supreme syllable, which is composed of the qualities of rajas, sattva, and tamas, endowed with three dots, and consists of all the gods.
O lady of beautiful limbs, listen to the syllable *sa*, the seed-mantra of Śakti, which is higher than the highest;
it has the form of ten million streaks of lightning and is joined with the three Kuṇḍalīs. (6.15)
O Goddess, it is always composed of the five deities and always composed of the five vital breaths;
it is joined with rajas, sattva, and tamas, and is always endowed with the three points (bindus).
Having prostrated constantly, O Goddess, contemplate within your heart, O beautiful one, the syllable accompanied by the three powers and joined with the principles beginning with the Self. 6/17
Listen to the letter *ha*, O lady of beautiful limbs, which bestows the fourfold aims of human life;
it is joined with the three *kuṇḍalīs* and resembles a streak of red lightning. (6.18)
The letter is always joined with rajas, sattva, and tamas; it consists eternally of the five deities, has the nature of the five vital breaths, and is always accompanied by the three powers.
O beautiful one, contemplate the syllable accompanied by three dots within your heart;
O lady of lovely limbs, hear the letter *kṣa*, which is joined with the triad of Kuṇḍalīs.
The phoneme consists eternally of the four aims of human life and the five deities;
the phoneme consists eternally of the five vital breaths and is accompanied by the three powers.
O beautiful one, meditate in your heart upon the syllable accompanied by three dots, conjoined with the principles beginning with Ātman, resembling the autumnal moon. (6.22)
From the letter 'A' to the letter 'Kṣa', she herself is the supreme Kuṇḍalinī;
from the phonemes, the entire universe of moving and non-moving beings is certainly born. (6.23)
O beautiful one, various treatises, the Purāṇas, the Itihāsas, the Vedas, the Smṛti scriptures, and whatever others there may be— || 6/24 ||
"From the Imperishable (Akṣara) everything is born; it is the Supreme Brahman itself, O Beloved.
Thus ends the sixth chapter in the *Kāmadhenu Tantra*, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The seventh chapter. Śrī Mahādeva said:
This supreme mystery, most wonderful, has always resided within my heart.
Henceforth, I shall explain the reality of mantra individually. (7.1)
O Varārohā, listen attentively to the Mātṛkā;
thereafter, one should recite the mantra and the fifty Mātṛkās separately. (7.2)
Therefore, you shall be qualified; no further deliberation is required in this matter.
Thus, O Goddess, I have explained to you this supreme mantra and its ritual application.
O Goddess, if a person recites his desired mantra without this mantra, everything for him shall be in vain; it is all a futile exertion. (7.4)
O Dear One, one should first recite this mantra ten times;
thereafter, having uttered the *praṇava*, one should recite the *mātṛkā* individually.
Listen attentively to this most wonderful practice.

It is as follows: Oṃ, a/ oṃ; oṃ, āṃ oṃ; oṃ, i/ oṃ; oṃ, ī/ oṃ; oṃ, u/ oṃ; oṃ, ū/ oṃ; oṃ, ṛ/ oṃ; oṃ, ṝ/ oṃ; oṃ, ḷ/ oṃ; oṃ, ḹ oṃ; oṃ, e/ oṃ; oṃ, ai/ oṃ; oṃ, o/ oṃ; oṃ, au/ oṃ; oṃ, aṃ oṃ; oṃ, aḥ oṃ; oṃ, kaṃ oṃ.
In this manner, O lady of beautiful limbs, one should always recite each syllable up to the letter *kṣa*, encased by the *praṇava* (OM),
ten times each.
One should perform meditation on each [syllable] individually by means of recitation alone;
or else, O fair-faced one, having combined all the syllables together.
One should mutter the mantra ten times; thereafter, one should mutter one's own specific mantra.
Likewise, I shall describe the meditation for all castes; listen attentively. (7.8)
Resembling ten million moons, seated upon a white lotus, possessing the playful luster of wandering bees, and adorned with three eyes. (7.9)
The Goddess, who is always composed of the practice of various sciences and is the expounder of diverse scriptures, consists of manifold musical instruments and is adorned with white garments. (7.10)
O Pārvatī, her limbs were radiant with white ornaments, she wore a white upper garment,
and in the mirror held in her left hand was the entire universe.
In the same way, having meditated upon Mātṛkā, the Mother of the World and Sustainer of the Universe, she is called the "small mirror" (kṣudradarpaṇa) when one beholds her as a young parrot. (7.12)
Whoever recites the mantra ten times or even once attains all accomplishments; there is no need for deliberation on this point. (7.13)
This supreme Mātṛkā-vidyā has been declared to you;
by practicing it, the adept attains the rare and imperishable liberation. (7.14)
Or else, O Goddess, O lovely-faced one, [one may worship] each one individually;
listen to this secret, O fair-limbed one, which is most hidden throughout the three worlds. (7.15)
O Supreme Goddess, having once recollected the desired Vidyā with the mind,
O Goddess, one should diligently perform the meditation (dhyāna) appropriate for whichever mantra it may be.
O Dear One, having recited that mantra ten times, one should then perform the meditation on the desired deity;
indeed, by reciting the mantra of the desired deity, one shall thereafter obtain all accomplishments.
By this method, O Goddess, the mantra shall attain consciousness;
for a mantra or a vidyā devoid of consciousness, O worshipful one of the gods, [is ineffective]. (7.18)
"O Goddess, everything would become useless; that recitation would be fruitless.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
"Listen further, O lady of beautiful limbs, to the unsurpassed eightfold group of letters (vargāṣṭaka). (7.19)
O Goddess, if one performs ten million recitations (koṭi-puraścaraṇa) without the eight groups [of mantras], all of that is in vain, O Goddess, and in the end he shall go to hell. (7.20)
The eight groups of consonants are a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, and śa.
At the beginning and at the end of the mantra, there should be the letter 'a' joined with the bindu (anusvāra). (7.21)
Having given that very [offering] with devotion, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times;
by this procedure, O Goddess, one should perform the rite of Ādityābha.
O fair-limbed one, one should recite [the mantra] until one hundred thousand repetitions are completed;
then, O fair-limbed one, by means of this mantra, one will certainly attain longevity. (7.23)
O Goddess, one should not perform the *puraścaraṇa* without being alive; O Goddess, if one were to perform the *puraścaraṇa* without being alive— (7.24)
All that [merit] of his becomes fruitless, and his prior merit perishes;
therefore, one should recite [the mantra] a hundred times every day together with the eight groups. 7/25.
O auspicious lady, for such a person, every mantra is always and instantly accomplished;
what need is there then for meditation, worship, or the preliminary ritual service (puraścaraṇa)? (7.26)
O lady of excellent complexion, having performed the vitalization (*jīvana*) of the mantra and the *vidyā*,
O Goddess, he who likewise performs the determination of the life-force (*prāṇanirṇaya*) for the *vidyā*— [7.27]
O lady of beautiful limbs, at that very moment, hundreds upon hundreds attain the fruit of *puraścaryā*, especially in the Kali Yuga within Bhārata, the land of Jambūdvīpa. (7.28)
O Goddess, without the placement of the vital breaths (prāṇanyāsa), a practitioner should never recite mantras—whether Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, or Śākta. (7.29)

O Dear One, the placement of the vital breaths (prāṇanyāsa) is highly recommended for the mantras of Gaṇeśa and Saura; what need is there to mention its efficacy in his recitations, worship, fire-offerings, and so forth?
O Maheśānī, he who knows the principle of vital breath (prāṇatattva) is a true worshiper;
O Goddess, he who performs the ritual placement on the body (dehanyāsa) without the principle of vital breath [is not]. (7.31)
He is fallen and most sinful; he shall go to the Raurava hell.
O Goddess, having gazed upon his face, one should perform the ritual of beholding the sun.
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the *Kāmadhenu-tantra*, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The eighth chapter: Śrī Mahādeva said:
This most wonderful secret has been told to you, O blessed lady, which has not been spoken individually for each Mātṛkā in any of the Tantras. (8.1)
The convention of the fifty letters is the supreme fiftyfold reality;
that reality consists of all the gods and likewise consists of all knowledge. (8.2)
O Goddess, it consists of the principle of the Bindu, likewise of the principle of Ahaṃ;
it is the principle consisting of all powers, and likewise consisting of all vital breaths. (8.3)
O Goddess, it consists of the reality of the embryo and is likewise merely a bud;
O Goddess, when the bud of a flower is endowed with fragrance, [it is so]. (8.4)
O lady of pure smiles, the fragrance is likewise invisible to all beings, just as light shines within the bud of a flower. (8.5)
In that very same way, the nine principles (navatattva) are contained within the seed-syllable *kalikā*; I bow down to Mātṛkā, who resembles ten million flashes of lightning. (8.6)
She is free from affliction and devoid of qualities, yet she is the source of all qualities;
she is the mother of all sciences and is established in all the sacred scriptures.
O Pārvatī, O Goddess, she is praised as the mother of all the sciences of the Vedas and of all the cosmic eggs; she is also the fifty Mātṛkās.
The reality of mantra and the Vidyā, the definitive determination of all phonemes, Mātṛkā in the form of fifty young women, the imperishable Śava. 8.9.
O Supreme Goddess, Mātṛkā is Kālī herself; of this there is no doubt.
Where is Brahmā, where is Viṣṇu, and where is Rudra the Lord? (8.10)
"O Goddess, O Beloved, why are all those [deities], including Sadāśiva, like corpses?
All the gods are like corpses, and the entire universe is always like a corpse. (8.11)
For this very reason, O Varārohā, just as it is with the mantra of Viṣṇu, so it is with the mantra of Śiva, O Goddess, as well as that of Gaṇeśa and Sūrya. (8.12)
The Śakti-mantra and the Vidyā consisting of fifty young women, as well as the Purāṇas, the Vedas, and likewise the Smṛti-śāstras. (8.13)
O lady of excellent hips, this is the wondrous reality in the form of a young woman;
[it is] Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva. (8.14)
O beloved one with tremulous eyes, all of them are born from Mātṛkā;
O Goddess, Mātṛkā is the mother of all, the supreme progenitor. (8.15)
The Great Power (Mahāśakti) is celebrated as being endowed with hundreds of thousands of sidelong glances;
O Dear One, the universe devoid of the letters of the Mother (Mātṛkā) is like a corpse.
Song, instrumental music, hearing, drama, and conversation—O woman of excellent complexion, for every form of youth is established upon the path of meditation. (8.17)
Thus has been told to you, O Goddess, the supreme seed-syllable of Kālikā;
through the union of both, O Beloved, it becomes fully blossomed. (8.18)
O Goddess, at the confluence, many attain the blossoming, imperishable liberation—that which certainly does not blossom through mantras or branches of knowledge. (8.19)
Listen, O lady of beautiful limbs: one should perform the sacrifice of recitation (*japayajña*) with full blossoming;
for if, O dear Goddess, the mantra of knowledge is devoid of blossoming, [it is ineffective]. (8.20)
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, one attains accomplishment only by meditating upon the seed-syllable of Kālikā with each individual letter separately; it is not otherwise. 8.21
From a full-blown flower or even from a bud, Kṛṣṇa and the others certainly arise;
she who is called the young woman is the supreme Mahākuṇḍalī.
The goddess Kuṇḍalinī, the supreme deity, consists of color and form;
he who recites the mantra of the Vidyā, which is the essence of the fifty letters, [attains success]. (8.23)
For all that is fruitless for him; his recitation would be like a corpse.
O Goddess, that recitation devoid of consciousness is indeed a corpse itself. (8.24)
Having known this and having prostrated, O beloved, one should perform recitation, worship, and other rites;
for Hari is indeed directly devoid of attributes (nirguṇa), while the supreme Kuṇḍalinī possesses attributes (saguṇā).
Therefore, from that youthful body, the very birth of Hari occurred;
it is always the seed and the place of birth for all the gods and goddesses.
From the seed is born Brahmā, the eternal one whose form is emptiness;
for this very reason, O Maheśānī, she is the supreme cause of Brahmā. (8.27)

O Goddess, he who performs recitation and worship after knowing this tantra, and he who performs recitation and worship after having performed the ritual of the placement of the vital breaths (prāṇanyāsa); || 8/28 ||
He is Śiva, the supreme Brahman; he alone is Puruṣottama;
he alone is the divine Vīra, and he himself is Bhairava. (8.29)
O Goddess of the gods, he alone is blessed in the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile;
O Goddess, he is the Sun and the true Guru, and not otherwise. (8.30)
He alone is capable of both elevating and destroying, and not otherwise;
for he who performs the sacrifice of recitation (japayajña) without knowing this tantra [is ineffective]. (8.31)
"O Goddess, all of that is in vain for him; he is merely a beast, there is no doubt.
And among all [beings], O Goddess, the disciple is always like a beast before the guru. (8.32)

O daughter of the mountain, O lady of beautiful limbs, if one hears the knowledge or the mantra from his mouth, he becomes as if sprinkled [with consecration]; what need has he for recitation or worship? (8.33)
O Dear One, having heard such [teachings] from the mouth of a beast, one should abandon a guru of this kind,
renounce the previous mantra, and take up another belonging to the Gaṇas.
He is fallen and he is most wicked; how can we worship the mantra?
O Goddess, whatever sin a man might incur from the mere counting of the mantra— (8.35)
Listen, O lady of beautiful limbs, to that sin and to the successive hells that one would incur, O Goddess, by shaking a self-manifested liṅga (svayaṃbhū-liṅga). (8.36)
That sin is multiplied ten millionfold by the counting of divine mantras;
therefore, O Goddess, a wise person should avoid counting them. (8.37)
Having abandoned [the study] among the Śaivas, Vaiṣṇavas, Sauras, and likewise the Gāṇapatyas, a man should avoid counting it among any other sciences whatsoever. (8.38)
Thus ends the eighth chapter in the *Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra*, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The Ninth Chapter.
The illustrious Mahādeva said: Now I shall fully declare the secret, the most excellent mystery.
Having known which, the practitioner goes to the rare abode of Brahmā. (9.1)

O Beloved, one should fill the breath through the iḍā and then draw it into the interior of the suṣumnā; subsequently, one should exhale it through the path of the piṅgalā according to the sequence of prāṇāyāma.
O fair-limbed one, one should meditate upon the youthful Mother (Mātṛkā) in her direct order;
[one should contemplate] the fifty letters of the Mātṛkā, together with the bindu and joined with the nāda.
Having uttered [the mantra] with the inhalation (pūraka) alone, one should then recite the desired [mantra].
Thereafter, O Dear One, one should mutter the letters of the Mātṛkā in reverse order.
In the middle region of the Suṣumnā, O lady of beautiful countenance,
one should meditate upon the youthful Mātṛkā, both in direct and reverse order.
Then, having recited the chosen mantra, diligently perform it in reverse;
by this very procedure, one should exhale through the path of Piṅgalā.
O woman of excellent complexion, O lady with tremulous eyes, O lotus-faced one, he who performs this in twelve ways every day at the three junctions of the day— 9.7.
For him, there shall be the placement of life-force (jīvanyāsa) and the perfection of mantra; it is not otherwise.
O Maheśānī, in the Kali age, the number [of repetitions] is fourfold compared to that of one time.
"By performing this ten times every day, a man shall become equal to Śiva.
Thus ends the ninth chapter in the *Śrīkāmadhenu-tantra*, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The Tenth Chapter. Śrī Mahādeva said:
O lovely-limbed one, O beloved, the principle of the forehead is always the letter *A*.
O lady of excellent complexion, listen now to the form which is the true essence of the face.
The letter *i* is the right eye, and the letter *ī* is in the left eye;
the letter *u* should be in the right ear, and the letter *ū* in the left ear. (10.2)
The syllable *ṛ* is the right nostril, and the syllable *ṝ* is the left nostril;
the syllable *ḷ* is the right cheek, and the syllable *ḹ* is the left cheek. (10.3)
The letter *e* is the lower reality (*tattva*), and *ai* is the lip;
*o* is the upper tooth, and *au* is the lower tooth. (10.4)
The syllable *Aṃ* is the reality of the head, and the syllable *Aḥ* is the circle of the face;
the five principles beginning with the letter *Ka* are praised as being on the right arm. (10.5)
On the left arm, the five principles beginning with the letter *ca* reside;
and on the right foot, O fair-faced one, the five principles beginning with the letter *ṭa*.
The five principles beginning with the letter *ta* are praised in the left foot;
the letter *pa* is on the right side, and the letter *pha* is on the left side. (10.7)
The letter *ba* is the principle of the back, the letter *bha* is the navel, the letter *ma* is the principle of the belly, and likewise the letter *ya* is the heart. (10.8)
The letter *ra* is the principle of Skanda, and the letter *la* is Vāma;
the letter *va* is the principle of Ghaṭa, and the letter *śa* is on the right arms. (10.9)
The syllable *ṣa* on the left arm, *sa* on the right foot, *ha* on the left foot, and *kṣa* above the head. (10.10)
The seed-principle *akāra* and the letter *takāra* together with the *praṇava*, as well as *makāra* and *sakāra*, are likewise adorned. || 10/11 ||
The syllable *pa* is the ego (*ahaṅkāra*), and likewise the syllable *pha* is the mind (*manas*).
The syllable *na* is the principle of sound (*śabdatattva*), and the syllables *da* and *dha* are praised as form (*rūpa*). (10.12)
The letter *ga* is the principle of the feet, and the letter *cha* is the generative organ (*upastha*);
the letter *u* is the principle of space (*ākāśa*), and the letter *ū* is the sense of hearing (*śrotra*). || 10.13 ||
The letter *ja* shall be the principle of the skin (*tvaktattva*), and *jha* shall be the feet;
*ka* is the principle of the earth (*pṛthvītattva*), and *kha* is the principle of knowledge (*jñānatattva*).
The syllable Śa is the heart-lotus; the syllable Ṣa is the circle of reality (tattvamaṇḍala);
likewise, the syllable Sa is the moon, and the syllable Ra is the fire-circle.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, the syllable *ṣa* is the supreme reality (*parameṣṭhi-tattva*),
while the syllable *la* is the earth element (*pṛthvī-tattva*) and the syllable *ha* is likewise the head.
The letter *ya* is the wind element (*vāyutattva*), and the letter *ka* is heaven itself;
having attained the union of these two, the letter *kṣa* is the embodiment of all principles (*tattva*).

Therefore, O Sulocanā, the letters beginning with *a* and ending with *kṣa*—namely *a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ḹ, e, ai, o, au, aṃ, aḥ*, as well as *ta, tha, da, dha, na, pa, pha, ba, bha, ma, sa, pa, pha, na, da, dha, ga, cha, u, ū, ja, jha, ka, kha, śa, ṣa, sa, ra, ya, la, ha, kṣa*—constitute the twenty-five principles (*tattvas*).
This supreme self, which is all principles, is most secret. (10.18)
O Varārohā, listen now to the names of the Mātṛkās in their proper order:
Brahmāṇī, Caṇḍikā, Raudrī, Gaurī, and likewise Indrāṇī. (10.19)
Kaumāro, Vaiṣṇavī, Durgā, as well as Nārasiṃhikā, Kālikā, Muṇḍamālā, Śivadūtī, and likewise Parā. (10.20)
O beloved, [these are] Varāhī, Kauṣikī, as well as Māheśvarī, Śaṅkarī, Jayantī, Maṅgalā, and Kalimardinī. || 10/21 ||
Pālikā, Medhā, Śivarūpā, and Śāmbhavī;
Bhīmā, Śāntā, Ugrā, Bhrāmarī, and Rudrarūpiṇī. (10.22)
Ambikā, Bahurūpā, Kṣemā, and likewise Kṣemaṅkarī;
she who takes the form of Dhātrī, Svadhā, Svāhā, and likewise she who has the form of Vahni.
Aparṇā, Māyā, Ghorarūpā, Priyaṃvadā, Brahmāṇḍavāṇī, and Brāhmī—these are remembered as the fifty Mātṛkās. || 10/24 ||
Thus, this has been fully related to you out of devotion;
these indeed are the Mātṛkā goddesses, who constitute the cosmic egg with all its moving and unmoving beings.
O lady of beautiful limbs, those imperishable ones, assuming various forms, abide pervading the Śakti-mantra,
the Viṣṇu-mantra, the Śiva-mantra, and the Saura-mantra, O Pārvatī.
O lady of excellent complexion, in all other mantras as well as in those of Gaṇeśa,
Mātṛkā exists in the form of a young woman, whose very body is the mantra.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—all these, O lady of tremulous glances, are motionless and devoid of senses. (10.28)
O lady of excellent hips, for the gods and others there is never a mantra;
when the Śabdabrahman enters the Tantra, it then becomes a mantra.
All fifty young women are of the nature of the Sound-Brahman (Śabdabrahman). O noble lady, there is no cause for Brahman; however, there is a cause for Prakṛti.
O lady of beautiful hips, that which arises from *prakṛti* is the initiation (*dīkṣā*) approved by all;
and in this initiation, O lady with tremulous glances, the art of youth is highly praised. (10.31)
That which consists of the fifty Mātṛkās is celebrated as the Youthful One (Yuvati).
O Goddess, without the Youthful One, where is the Vidyā? Where is the Mantra?
The Supreme Brahman is devoid of qualities; the hosts of Youthful Ones are its primary manifestation.
Thus ends the tenth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The eleventh chapter.
Śrī Śiva said:
Just as the solar principle (sūryatattva) exists in water, so too is it established within the mantra.
The clusters of light of the goddesses exist as the digits of Prakṛti. || 11.1 ||
Then, O lady of beautiful countenance, the inner self is the supreme knower;
sixteen forms of youth abide [therein], which are higher than primordial nature (prakṛti).
For, O Goddess, even the eternal Brahmā is a knower only apart from Prakṛti;
therefore, O lady of beautiful hips, he alone is Śrī Sadāśiva. || 11/3 ||
O woman of excellent complexion, she who is waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, as well as the fourth state— O lady of beautiful hips, all those states are that supreme, transcendent young woman.
And at the time of cause and effect, O fair-faced one, it is to be reckoned as follows:
from the void comes the void, the supreme void, the form of the void, which is stainless. (11.5)
O lady of beautiful limbs, contemplate within your heart that supreme, stainless knowledge, which resembles ten million suns—a mass of light of great splendor. (11.6)

O fair-faced one, he possesses the luster of a mass of crushed añjana, is the king of colors, has a form made graceful by the three bends [of the body], and is resplendent with a beautiful crest-lock. || 11.7 ||
His crest is joined with a peacock’s tail and is most beautifully adorned by bees;
he is clothed in yellow garments and decorated with a forest garland.
Adorned with jeweled earrings, his cheeks were radiant and captivating; his ears, graced by *kadamba* flowers, enchanted all who beheld him. (11.9)
Resplendent with the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem, adorned with arms reaching down to his knees,
with a pair of reddish eyes, and possessing a brilliance equal to ten million flashes of lightning.
His pair of feet were slightly reddened and accompanied by the tinkling of anklets;
his palms were clear and slightly reddened, and he was resplendent with a garland of *guñjā* berries.
O fair-faced one, Viṣṇu, who consists of the Brahman of sound, arose in the center of the heart in the form of the syllable *ikāra*, which is uttered as sound.
O fair-eyed one, she is born from the seed-syllable of desire (Kāma-bīja) in the midst of the void;
O Goddess, she abides in the midst of the void, having the very nature of the seed-syllable of desire.
She who is conjoined with the letter *la* is celebrated as the Mother of Kṛṣṇa;
among all the mantras of Viṣṇu, the seed-syllable of desire (*kāma-bīja*) is the highest of the high.
O Maheśānī, O beloved, one should mutter the mantra of Viṣṇu within the empty heart;
from that very seed-syllable of desire (Kāma-bīja), the form of Viṣṇu arises.
Therefore, O Pārvatī, meditate upon Viṣṇu, who consists of desire, within your heart;
for she who is the passionate woman, O Maheśānī, is celebrated as the mother of Viṣṇu.
Therefore, one shall attain Viṣṇu, the color of the Mother, the king of letters.
The letter *ka* is Kāminī herself; the letter *la* is Pṛthivīśvarī. (11.17)
Rati is Mardinī herself, while Nāda is the form of the Yoni;
Bindu is the form of Kuṇḍalinī, consisting of Śiva and Śakti, O beloved. (11.18)
O Great Goddess, this seed-syllable is the mother of Viṣṇu, the supreme syllable;
for the god Viṣṇu is indeed beyond syllables, yet he is certainly born from the syllable. (11.19)
Therefore, O Varārohā, the supreme [energy] is the cause of Brahmā;
she who exists in the form of the seed-syllable *klīṃ* is celebrated as the Supreme (*parā*).
She, who is even higher than the highest, is also conjoined with the circle of fire;
she is Kāminī, O Maheśānī, and the earth is her seat.
Sometimes she dwells in the midst of the earth, sometimes in the circle of fire;
the goddess Kāminī resides there, endowed with the three drops.
O beloved, Mahāviṣṇu, having attained birth, should mutter the *kūrca* seed-syllable;
by this means, O lady of excellent complexion, he should recite the *huṃkāra* mantra.
In the act of assuming that body of Viṣṇu, she herself was the embodiment of primordial nature (prakṛti);
O daughter of the mountain, Prakṛti is the supreme object of worship for the gods.
O beloved, listen to the syllable *huṃ*, the most wonderful seed-syllable at the end:
it is the sixth vowel, its companion is the sky-seed (*ha*), and it has the luster of the moon. (11.25)
O lady of excellent hips, visualize above that [the syllable] always with a bindu—the [syllables] known as Kāma, Manmatha, Kandarpa, and Akṣaradhvaja. (11.26)
O Maheśānī, the Fish-bannered One (Kāmadeva) is proclaimed as the five seed-syllables:
Māyā, Kūrca, Vadhū, and Lakṣmī, O Pārvatī. (11.27)
And the Praṇava, O Maheśānī, as well as the fourteenth [vowel] itself, exists together with the Piṇḍas, O Goddess, in those [mantras] and in those [mudrās]. (11.28)
That mantra becomes perfected through the mind; the Supreme is of the nature of primordial matter (prakṛti).
Having meditated thus upon the seed-syllable even once, one becomes beloved by all. (11.29)
One should mutter that mantra, O Goddess, and again perform the visualization of the seed-syllable, O Dear One;
for in this way, one performs the seed-syllable practice of the mantras ten times.
Having drawn forth from that seed-syllable the arising form of the deity, and having then performed meditation on the deity, one should subsequently recite the desired mantra. (11.31)
O beloved, perform meditation on the deity once more, and again perform the recitation;
indeed, having performed it ten times in this manner, there shall be the very empowerment of the deity.
Then, having recited the Saptacchada mantra, one should recite the Kulluka ten times;
having placed the Setu mantra at the beginning and the end, one should recite it one hundred and eight times.
O Goddess, one should recite that mantra in this way to attain accomplishment.
Thus ends the eleventh chapter in the *Kāmadhenu-tantra*, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The twelfth chapter.
The venerable Mahādeva said:
I shall proclaim another secret, one that is most strictly concealed.
And without having performed the reality of meditation, as well as the eightfold reality.
Without performing [the rite], it goes to waste; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
Thereafter, the mantra attains the state of being "living" and becomes effective at that very moment. (12.2)
Alternatively, O Supreme Goddess, having encased the syllables of the mantra in the *praṇava* (Oṃ) in both direct and reverse order, [one should recite it]. || 12.3 ||
At that very moment, O Supreme Goddess, the mantra attains the state of being alive,
whether it be made single-fold or three-fold, O fair-faced one, if one should perform [it].
Then one attains success, O Goddess worshipped by the gods, and not otherwise;
for if a wise person should mutter the mantra without [the state of] being alive, O Goddess. (12.5)
O lady of tremulous glances, for one who recites that mantra, there is no doubt that he is like a corpse; O Pārvatī, such a practitioner is always overcome by sleep and is devoid of life.
Śrīṃ klīṃ hrīṃ huṃ strīṃ śrīṃ oṃ.
O lady of excellent complexion, how does one attain success while asleep?
O fair-limbed one, by means of the *jīvanyāsa*, the breaking of sleep will certainly occur. (12.7)

Then, O beautiful one, having recited the principle of the drop (bindu-tattva) and the principle of knowledge (jñāna-tattva), as well as the principle of vital breath (prāṇa-tattva) and likewise the principle of the deity (deva-tattva), O lady of lovely limbs. (12.8)
O fair-eyed goddess, if one should mutter prayers without knowing the reality of recitation, the reality of mantra, and the reality of meditation in every syllable, O Goddess; (12.9)
That which becomes a union is declared to be the "blooming" (praphulla);
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, that alone is the seed-syllable of the bud (kalikābīja). 12.10
"That which has come from my mouth and always enters your mouth is the thought of Śrī Vāsudeva; thus it has been told to you, O beloved. (12.11)
This mantra is a great secret, joined with the face of Īśāna;
indeed, by the power of this mantra, I drink the Kālakūṭa poison.
These letters of the Mātṛkās reside within the center of the Suṣumṇā;
O lady of beautiful hips, these letters are always composed of the Great Yoga.
"O Goddess, O beautiful one, without the syllable (akṣara), yoga does not arise for me—whether on the path of yoga, the path of devotion, or the path of liberation. (12.14)
In the path of meditation, in worship, and likewise in the path of recitation,
these young women are the forms of both cause and effect.
Without knowing this mantra, one should never recite it;
likewise, without knowing this mantra, one should not study the Purāṇas, the Saṃhitās, or the Smṛtis.
By reciting it, one goes to hell along with one's ancestors; it is not otherwise.
Whatever merit exists in all dharmas and whatever fruit exists in all sacrifices [is obtained by this]. (12.17)
Whatever fruit a twice-born man may obtain from all gifts and sacred fords,
he attains that same fruit merely by meditating upon the castes.
One who recites the Purāṇas without understanding the meditation on the phonemes (varṇadhyāna) as well as the true nature of the phonemes (varṇatattva) will certainly go to hell. || 12.19 ||
Taking up ten million bamboos, that twice-born man would go to hell;
as is the speaker, so is the listener, for the fruit is equal for both.
How is it that a fool, out of ignorance and without knowing the determination of castes, would go to hell after reading the Purāṇas? (12.21)
O Great Goddess, one will certainly encounter terrible poverty;
indeed, one will certainly contract disease in Bhārata within Jambūdvīpa. (12.22)
He shall be the eternal God; Vāṇī is Tripurasundarī, and Bhavānī is the presiding deity of all young women.
One should meditate upon the Goddess Mahāmāyā, the Mother (Mātṛkā), the Sovereign of the Universe—
seated upon a red lotus throne and adorned with red garments.
Her limbs were smeared with red sandalwood paste, and she wore a red cloth as an upper garment;
she shone like a ripe bimba fruit, and her supreme face was like the full moon.
She was adorned with three eyes possessing the playful luster of wandering bees,
endowed with hundreds of sidelong glances, and graced by a beautiful crest-ornament.

Beautifully adorned with red ornaments, her form graced by the three-fold bend (tribhaṅgi), endowed with a smile and a blossoming face, she possesses a complexion like a mass of moonlight. || 12.27 ||
She was adorned with vine-like arms resembling lotus stalks, dressed in a beautiful bodice, and possessed breasts like *kadamba* buds. (12.28)
Deluding the world with the radiance of the rays from her nails—
thus one should meditate upon Mahāmāyā Bhavānī, the enchantress of Śiva.
I shall proclaim another secret, most wonderful and marvelous:
one should meditate upon [the deity] atop a boar within the twelve-petaled heart-lotus.

Having meditated upon the seed-syllable of whichever deity, as well as its fully blossomed bud, and having visualized the Goddess according to one's capacity, she shall manifest from that [syllable] of her own accord.
Whether it be Śakti, or Lord Viṣṇu, or Śiva, or even Sūrya—O Goddess, from the seed arises the supreme Brahman, the stainless one. (12.32)
O Goddess, without seed-meditation (*bījadhyāna*), how is Hari produced? How does Sadāśiva, the Great God, manifest himself? (12.33)
"She who is the mother of Sadāśiva, eternal and in the form of the seed-syllable"—he who knows this is a man of knowledge, he alone is the most excellent of heroes. (12.34)
He alone is the worthy guru; he alone is the supreme Śiva.
One should perform meditation in this manner upon all the seed-syllables (bījas).
She has a form resembling white lightning, possesses three eyes,
is endowed with side-long glances as her arrows, and is equipped with four arms.
She is in a graceful posture with three bends, adorned with a beautiful crest,
seated upon a white lotus, possessing a face like the full moon, and supreme.
Her limbs were anointed with various perfumes, adorned with fragrant garlands,
her body radiant with various ornaments, and she was elegantly dressed in garments of cloud-like silk.
The primordial Goddess, composed of Brahman, who illumines the three worlds with the diversion of lute-playing, and whose nature is that of the desired seed-syllable.
I worship the goddess Mātṛkā, the eternal mother of the Vedas, at whose feet Brahmā and the other deities have fallen upon the earth. 12.40
Having meditated according to this method, one becomes beloved by all.
O Great Goddess, one should first recite this seed-syllable ten times.
O lady with tremulous glances, that mantra resides in the chapter on bliss;
having meditated upon it from there and then recited it ten times, O woman of excellent complexion.
O Pārvatī, if one should mutter [the mantra] without knowing this reality, that twice-born man will become filled with all manner of sins, like a pig. (12.43)
"This reality is a great secret, ever established on the path of yoga;
out of devotion to you, O fair-eyed one, I have declared this most profound mystery. (12.44)
This is the essence of the tantras, bestowing all accomplishments;
he is the yogi, the knower of yoga, the soul of yoga, and the leader of yoga.
The teacher of yoga, the master of yogic illusion, the bestower of the bliss of yoga. || 12/45 ||
Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The thirteenth chapter.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
Now, O beloved, I shall fully proclaim the Chapter on Bliss (Ānandapaṭala).
Listen, I shall proclaim the truth, which is beautiful and most enchanting. (13.1)

One should contemplate the seed-syllables of the mantra within the twelve-petaled heart-lotus, which is endowed with the brilliance of ten million lightning flashes, [visualizing] whichever deity is one's chosen deity.
O Pārvatī, one should first meditate upon the seed-syllable atop a cowrie shell;
all other seed-syllables should be placed individually in the middle of each petal.
Having thus recited ten times, O Dear One, one should then recite the seed-syllable in sequence;
O Goddess, one should recite the supreme seed-syllable ten times for each of those ten.
Then, O fair-eyed one, one should meditate upon the desired deity within the seed-syllable;
from that seed-syllable, O lady of excellent hips, the deity certainly arises. (13.5)
O lady of beautiful limbs, O beloved, having gazed upon the beauty of that god’s body from his feet to the tips of his hair, which was composed of various divine manifestations; 13.6.
Having observed [the deity] with devotion in the mind, one should again practice meditation;
thereafter, one should mutter the seed-syllable, which is the very nature of the bliss of the letters.
One should first recite the seed-syllable, and after that, perform the meditation on the seed-syllable.
This first seed-syllable practice is difficult to attain, O beloved. (13.8)
If the practitioner knows the meditation, which is supremely auspicious, for all the seed-syllables, individually for each and every syllable; (13.9)
O lady of tremulous glances, if one should practice the meditation on the Mātṛkās without knowing [this],
O Goddess, that very same result certainly arises for all of them instantly.
One should meditate separately upon the specific color of each mantra;
from the seed-syllable (bīja), O beloved, Viṣṇu, the best of incarnations, is born.
From the seed Rāma is born; from the seed Kṛṣṇa is produced.
O Goddess, everything—both the stationary and the moving—is born from the seed. (13.12)
O beloved, [she resides] in the Ājñā-cakra and the Viśuddhi; then in the Mūlādhāra, O Goddess, and then in the Svādhiṣṭhāna and the Maṇipūra, O Pārvatī.
By this method, O Goddess, the best of practitioners should perform [this rite];
he who performs it every day is a perfected one (siddha) and is indeed Śiva himself. (13.14)
O Maheśānī, O beloved, for him who daily causes the six cakras to revolve with restless side-glances through practice, [the result] is like that of a flower, my dear.
"O beloved with tremulous glances, tell me: must one necessarily perform the meditation on the seed-syllable and the mantra separately within the heart at all times? (13.16)
Śrī herself is the eternal Goddess Prakṛti, the primordial seed-form;
she is the mother of the Eternal One, O beloved, and consists of all the castes. 13.17.
In the first stage of recitation, one should utter the reality (tattva) of the seed-syllable;
thereafter, O fair-complexioned lady, one should recite the mantra together with its "bridge" (setu).
If one should mutter [the mantra] ten million times without knowing the reality of the seed-syllable, O Goddess, all of that is in vain, like weeping in the wilderness. (13.19)
O beautiful one, listen as I shall explain the three principles of mantras:
having visualized the seed-syllable of wind, together with its bindu, within the lotuses of the navel. (13.20)
O Maheśānī, having first meditated upon the seed-syllable of Vāyu in the center of the mantra, and having contemplated that seed-syllable, one should recite this supreme seed-syllable. (13.21)
One should recite the seed-syllable ten times and likewise perform meditation ten times;
at that very moment, the mantra becomes instantly endowed with the ten principles.
Having dried up the seed, O lady of beautiful limbs, one should indeed contemplate it within the fire-seed;
having meditated upon the seed of the consumer of oblations in the center of the fire within the heart-lotus. (13.23)
One should recite the mantra ten times and likewise perform meditation ten times;
then the mantra becomes instantly endowed with twenty principles.
Then, O Goddess, with a stream of nectar flowing from the sound of the Mother-mantra, one should drench the seed-syllable together with all its limbs, O lady of beautiful form. (13.25)
At that very moment, O beloved, having suddenly placed it upon the forehead in the abode of Varuṇa, one should meditate upon that seed-syllable in the center of Varuṇa.
Having recited it ten times, one should indeed contemplate the seed-syllable ten times;
then, O Dear One, that seed-syllable suddenly becomes composed of nectar.
O Goddess of the gods, one should meditate [on the syllable] within the Viṣṇu-mantras and within the lunar seed-syllables;
in all other mantras, one should meditate upon it in the abode of Varuṇa.
At that very moment, O Dear One, the mantra becomes endowed with thirty principles;
O Dear One, one should recite the Vidyā with speech, transcending the principles and transcending one's own nature.
O Dear One, that recitation which is devoid of the prescribed rite is always fruitless;
and he who recites it devoid of the essential reality is likewise perpetually fruitless.
O Goddess, drying up and burning—this is what is known as the nectar of knowledge;
O auspicious one, this consists of the ultimate reality and swiftly bestows accomplishment. (13.31)
Whoever recites [a mantra] devoid of the reality (tattva) suffers loss at every step;
therefore, having propitiated the auspicious reality, the wise person should then recite the mantra. (13.32)
O Goddess, by this method, one [should employ] the mantra consisting of all principles (tattva) for the mantras of Kṛṣṇa, the Rāmas, and the best of incarnations.
O Goddess, O beloved one of beautiful limbs, [this applies] to the Śākta mantra of Gaṇapati himself,
as well as to the mantras of Śiva and likewise to other tantras.
O Sulocanā, having joined the mantra with the thirty principles (tattvas) as its seed-syllable (bīja),
one shall attain the state of life within that seed-syllable by means of this very procedure.
Therefore, O beautiful lady, from that seed Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others are born; it is not otherwise, O fair-complexioned one. (13.36)
Having performed this mantra once, one should mutter the mantra incessantly;
one should mutter the vidyā incessantly and need not observe purity or impurity. (13.37)

O Dear One, a person may conceive of the mantra as being composed of letters; O Lady of Excellent Limbs, they conceive of the guru as a human being, and they conceive of the deity as a mere image. (13.38)
"What is the use of his recitation and worship? Everything is a futile torment.
Thus, O Goddess, I have explained to you the secret principle of the seed-syllable (bīja), which is well-guarded.
If you desire your own welfare, this knowledge must never be spoken to anyone;
for how could one who lacks this understanding attain the status of a guru? (13.40)
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The fourteenth chapter.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O deliverer from the ocean of worldly existence!
O Īśāna, please tell me the supreme reality of the letter *va*.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
O lady of tremulous glances, I have previously explained the supreme reality of Gāyatrī;
O beautiful woman, that Gāyatrī is endowed with four faces.
Meditate on the beloved letter Śa, along with the letter Va and Varuṇa, within the heart;
O Pārvatī, meditate on the Ya-group and the seed-syllable of Vāyu within the heart. (14.3)
O Goddess of the gods, that which belongs to the *ya*-group is called the seed-syllable of Vāyu;
that which is the fourth letter of the *ya*-group is proclaimed as the seed-syllable of Vāyu. (14.4)
The letter-group *ya* and the seed-syllable of wind (*y*)—this has been determined by me, O beloved;
meditate upon Varuṇa within all vidyās and mantras, O beloved. (14.5)
Meditate upon the labial consonants (Pavarga) joined with the wife of Vahni (the letter Ra) in the heart;
O Goddess, the Gāyatrī resides therein for the rite of expelling sins.
Meditative cultivation has been proclaimed according to the previously mentioned path of meditation;
O lovely-limbed one, O beloved, meditate upon the syllable *Va* through the distinctions of meditation.
Now I shall fully explain the supreme meditation on the letter *ka*; listen to its special feature, which I shall describe as being exceedingly difficult to attain. (14.8)
That which was not spoken in the Ānandapaṭala, I shall now tell you;
having meditated upon that, the practitioner attains the difficult-to-attain, imperishable liberation. (14.9)
By which kind of meditation the mantra and the tantra are accomplished;
by such mere meditation, a person becomes equal to Śiva. (14.10)
By the mere meditation on the letter *ka*, every syllable is indeed accomplished; and through the cultivation of the letter *ka*, the cultivation of all [syllables] occurs. (14.11)
Therefore, with every effort, contemplate the letter *ka* within your heart:
"Oṃ! [She who is] radiant like the morning sun, seated upon the back of a lion. (14.12)
Seated upon a red lotus, clothed in red garments, she has four arms and three eyes, and she holds five arrows and a bow. (14.13)
She grants boons and fearlessness, with full and lofty breasts,
and is encircled by four arms resembling lotus stalks in form.
She was resplendent with conch-shell bracelets, armlets, and bangles,
and her braid was beautified in its center by fragrant garlands of jasmine.
Her form is graced by the triple-bend (tribhaṅga) posture, adorned with a beautiful crest, her topknot joined with a peacock’s tail-feather and endowed with various jewels. || 14.16 ||
With a slightly smiling, serene countenance and a nose adorned with pearls,
she was resplendent with rows of teeth illuminated by the radiance of rubies.
With rows of nails possessing a luster like the full moon, unsurpassed,
and beautifully fashioned with jewels set in a necklace joined by golden threads.
Adorned with creeper-like eyebrows ignited by the arrows of her sidelong glances,
she is beautiful, endowed with the three sacred sites, and resplendent with three eyes.
Adorned with two thighs whose form was like that of the *rāmarambhā* plant, and beautified by jeweled filaments joined with great creepers. (14.20)
She was attended by the eight groups [of divine beings] and worshipped by the eight groups;
she was radiant with a tilaka of vermilion and her eyes were marked with collyrium.
It is white like the surface of a forehead, encircled by a crescent moon,
and that which is borne upon the head by the hosts of deities beginning with Brahmā.
O lady of excellent hips, if the practitioner meditates thus upon the beloved woman named Kāminī, who is the manifest embodiment of the preeminent letter *ka*, and then recites the mantra; 14.23.
At that very moment, O beautiful one, success arises for him suddenly.
O Goddess, one who is bound by worldly fetters (pāśava) should never perform recitation (japa) without knowledge of the phonemes (varṇa). 14.24
What need has he for hundreds upon hundreds of preparatory rites (puraścaryā) in the worship of meditation?
What need has he for recitation (japa) or fire-offerings (homa) on the lunar or solar festivals? (14.25)

O Goddess, without knowledge of the phonemes (varṇas), whether one be a Vaiṣṇava or a Śaiva, one should never utter [the mantra] at any time without knowing the illuminator of the phonemes (varṇadīpanī).
That which is proclaimed as the illuminator of all mantra-sciences is the most praised among all treatises: the Varṇadīpanī. (14.27)
O lady of pure smiles, having understood the Tantra, one should always perform initiation and worship for the Śakti-mantra, as well as for the Saura and Gāṇeśa mantras. (14.28)
Śrī Mahādeva said:
I shall speak there of a secret that must be kept strictly concealed; listen, for by performing it, the practitioner attains the supreme and most excellent state. (14.29)
O beloved, having applied a tilaka on the forehead with fragrant sandalwood, along with camphor, agallochum, musk, gorocana, and saffron; 14.30.
One should carefully apply a beautiful, clear, and heart-stealing *tilaka*, fashioned into a single, lovely triangle that enchants all people. (14.31)
Having combined them or even separately, one should have [the image] made from various substances:
one desiring sovereignty with red pigment, and one desiring liberation with white sandalwood.
O Goddess, for the purpose of subjugation (*vaśya*), the wise one should apply a forehead mark (*tilaka*) with yellow pigment (*rocana*);
and for the purpose of enchantment (*mohana*), O lady of tremulous glances, he should do so with aloe-wood, saffron, and other such substances.
O beautiful lady, one should apply black ointment on the forehead, the base of the arms, and likewise on both shoulders for the rite of slaying an enemy.
O beautiful one, [one should place them] on both sides of the heart-lotus, on the back, at the navel,
on the two thighs, on the two cheeks, and below on the two feet.
O Goddess, one should carefully inscribe the supreme syllable *ka*;
having joined it with the moon and the *bindu*, O lady of excellent complexion, one should inscribe it. (14.36)
At that very moment, O Goddess, the knowledge and the mantra are suddenly perfected;
it shall delude all the worlds and bring the chosen deity under one's control.
If one should recite [the mantra] once after having brought the chosen deity under control, O lady of tremulous glances, divinity arises at that very moment. (14.38)
O Goddess, for without divinity, whence can there be worship, and whence can there be recitation?
Otherwise, worship would be like that of a ghost, especially in the Vaiṣṇava tradition. (14.39)
O lady of pure smiles, having applied a tilaka of yellow pigment (rocanā) upon the forehead,
one should draw the most beautiful letter *ka* in its center.
This general *tilaka* has been described as enchanting to people;
indeed, this very *tilaka* shall even bring Keśava under one's control.
On the tenth day, one should begin the seat of recitation (japāsana) and continue it every day thereafter.
He who practices in this world without knowing these phonemes is fallen and most sinful; he shall go to the Raurava hell. (14.42)
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The Fifteenth Chapter.
The Holy Goddess said:
O God of gods, Mahādeva, Blue-throated One, Three-eyed One!
O Īśāna, if I am dear to you, tell me the truth of the heart.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the knowledge that is most difficult to attain;
by the mere realization of which, O beloved, one becomes Viṣṇu and a true Vaiṣṇava. (15.2)
The wise one should meditate on his own vidyā within the twelve-petaled heart-lotus;
O Pārvatī, he should first visualize the letter *ka* upon the pericarp.
Then, O Goddess, at each and every leaf, the wise one should mutter his own vidyā;
having first meditated upon the primary seed-syllable of the mantras, the wise one should mutter it. (15.4)
From that mantra, O Goddess, the form of the deity is born;
then, having meditated upon the deity by means of the path of meditation prescribed in the Tantra. (15.5)
O Goddess, meditation is threefold and bestows equal fruits;
having performed these three meditations in the heart-lotus, O Supreme Goddess. (15.6)

O Goddess, one should meditate upon one’s own vidyā within the central space inside the thousand-petaled lotus, as taught from the mouth of the Guru, having an appearance like ten million flashes of lightning.
One should meditate upon it incessantly with devotion, and one becomes perfected at that very moment.
O Goddess, from that seed-syllable are born those such as Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others.
O lady of tremulous glances, they all indeed arise from the seed;
having realized that eternal reality situated in the chapter on bliss. (15.9)
O lady of beautiful limbs, worship should be performed; it shall consist of all perfections.
Without knowing this eternal reality, one goes to hell. (15.10)
A Śūdra who, having heard knowledge or an excellent mantra from the mouth of a Śūdra, certainly falls into Raurava hell and whatever other hells there may be. (15.11)
One should not impart sacred knowledge to a Śūdra, nor should one ever accept it from a Śūdra;
for both, O Goddess, there is hell for ten million members of their lineage.
O Goddess, even a twice-born man who is of improper conduct becomes a guru to Śūdras if that Śūdra should be truthful and have his senses subdued. (15.13)
Having become devoted to the Dharma and having heard it from the mouth of his brahmin preceptor, he attains all perfections and shall swiftly reach the Divine. || 15.14 ||
In whatever land there exists a Śūdra who is a sinner and a seller of mantras, I consider that land to be fallen, and its king is likewise a sinner. (15.15)
O lady with tremulous eyes, how could he recite the mantra upon his tongue?
O beautiful woman, his tongue would be like urine, blood, and excrement. (15.16)
That mouth is a pit of urine and feces; its food is always equal to excrement;
and that water is manifest blood among those born of the same caste as outcasts.
Whatever sacred fords (tīrthas) exist upon the earth, which indeed consist of all the gods,
having beheld that sacred ford of his face, they depart, leaving that place behind.
Seeing his orb-like face, ten million sacred fords flee;
abandoning the waters of the Gaṅgā, they quickly reach their own abodes.
Those who are great sinners and those joined with such acts as the killing of a Brahmin—the Gaṅgā, the purifier of the three worlds, purifies them; of this there is no doubt. (15.20)
Śūdras who sell mantras always go to hell;
in the Kali age, they will indeed exist in the land of Bhārata—of this there is no doubt. (15.21)
Those who sell mantras are born as Śūdras in the wombs of tigers;
and any Brāhmaṇa who associates with them is indeed a leather-worker.
Even he who is devoted to his own duty, if he is a Śūdra who listens to sacred knowledge or mantras, is like a Cāṇḍāla; he is indeed a defiler of the social orders (varṇasaṅkara). || 15.23 ||
He is blessed in the midst of the earth; he alone is indeed the best of Vaiṣṇavas.
He is a devotee of Śakti, a devotee of Śiva, a devotee of Gaṇeśa, and likewise a devotee of Sūrya.
Thus, O Goddess, this determination of the knowledge of the letters has been told to you. || 15/24 ||
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Bliss of Knowledge," in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess within the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra.
The sixteenth chapter.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
I shall proclaim another secret, most wonderful and supreme.
O lady of tremulous glances, by performing which [rite], Rāvaṇa and the other night-stalkers [were subdued].
The Lord, the sovereign of the three worlds, attained unsurpassed growth and the supreme secret convention of the individual syllables. (16.2)
Hari, Brahmā, and Purandara know this truth;
listen attentively to the convention of the fifty letters. (16.3)
If a practitioner proceeds without having performed [the preliminary rites], he goes to the Raurava hell;
he enters the Raurava hell from which return is difficult to obtain. (16.4)
The best of Vaiṣṇavas should indeed perform the *viśeṣa* rite within the Viṣṇu-mantras;
for if he does not do so, the Vaiṣṇava goes to hell for millions upon millions of times. (16.5)
O beloved, O lady of excellent hips, month after month on Saturdays and Tuesdays, having performed the morning bath and completed the twilight devotions; || 16/6 ||
Then one should offer arghya to the Sun and perform the washing of his feet;
having entered the sacrificial pavilion and performed the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), [one should proceed].
One should perform the placement (nyāsa) of the Mātṛkā, and thereafter the breath control (prāṇāyāma);
then, O Pārvatī, one should perform other placements according to the path of the Tantra.
