Wearing white garments, adorned with garlands, and his body anointed with perfumes, he should take his seat upon a red cushion or, alternatively, a seat of kusha grass. (16.9)
Having smeared vermilion and red sandalwood upon copper vessels,
one should indeed inscribe the letters of the Mātṛkā alphabet individually within each of these vessels.

Having brought forth the face of Brahmā from its station within the great lotus, together with the vowels beginning with *a* and ending with *kṣa*, accompanied by the nasal bindu and joined with the moon. (16.11)
One should direct the breath through the path of the left nostril and cast it into the handful of flowers;
O lady of tremulous glances, one should then form a heap of those flowers.
Having meditated, one should worship the Goddess individually and in due order with various kinds of perfumes and likewise with various kinds of flowers.
O Goddess, with various kinds of incense and likewise with various kinds of lamps; O Goddess, with diverse food offerings consisting of the fourfold types.
Having offered various fruits and other items, one should worship the Supreme Goddess with necklaces made of diverse flowers and combined with fragrances such as *śukra* and others.
Standing within the Mahāpadma forest, one should recite the hundred and eight [syllables];
one should mutter the letters of the Mātṛkā, each letter individually and separately.
One should recite the mantra upon whichever lotus it resides;
staying within the forest, one should recite one's own vidyā a hundred times upon that very lotus.
O beloved, O fair-faced one, at that very moment she becomes perfectly propitious;
yet, if one fails to perform the worship of Mātṛkā month after month, [the result is otherwise].
O beloved, listen to the loss that befalls one who recites his desired mantra:
having entered the *citrā-nāḍī*, the Mātṛkā becomes the Sovereign of the World. (16.19)
O lady of excellent complexion, O Great Goddess, O beautiful one, [this applies] to all Vaiṣṇavas, Śāktas, Śaivas, and indeed others as well.
The Vaiṣṇavas and others indeed carry [the sacred thread]; my word is not otherwise.
The worship of the Mātṛkās is praised, as is initiation (dīkṣā) which comes from me alone.
O lady of beautiful limbs, the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) must indeed be performed separately for each [deity];
she is the mother of all vidyās and of all mantras, each individually. (16.22)
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, because from them knowledge and mantra arise, therefore, O Goddess, their worship is prescribed with great effort. (16.23)
Otherwise, worship performed for an entire year would be fruitless;
however, O Goddess, if one worships the Mātṛkā according to this rite, [it shall not be so]. (16.24)
The goddess Mātṛkā, being pleased, regards him as her own son;
even if he is devoid of the worship of Mātṛkā, he remains intent upon recitation and worship. (16.25)
For him, the Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), the Mother (Mātṛkā) and Sovereign of the World, carries away the splendor of his mantras, as well as his lifespan, knowledge, fame, and strength. (16.26)
I shall now declare another secret, most wonderful;
listen, O Pārvatī, as it is told in both direct and reverse order. (16.27)
O Maheśvarī, by practicing in both direct and reverse order in this very way,
one shall suddenly become a partaker of the fruits of all recitations and sacrifices.
One attains perfection suddenly; one attains dharma suddenly;
one attains wealth suddenly; one attains liberation suddenly. || 16/29 ||
He who, with a serene mind, performs this diligently month after month on the full moon and the new moon days— he indeed is Śrī Sadāśiva himself.
Having understood the illuminating science (vidyā) residing in the Ānanda-paṭala,
yet not knowing the illuminating science that bestows the fruits of the four aims of life—
this secret and everything else will become entirely fruitless. (16.31)
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The seventeenth chapter.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
"O beloved, without knowing this reality, spiritual disposition does not arise."
O Pārvatī, no deity exists in wood, nor does one exist in stone.
O Goddess, within all states of being exists that state which bears the nature of liberation;
the divine state and the heroic state shall always arise spontaneously. (17.2)
Otherwise, O goddess with tremulous eyes, one is always possessed of the nature of a beast;
O beloved, O Goddess, how could there be accomplishment without one's own true nature?
Therefore, O Goddess, one should diligently become possessed of the heroic state (vīrabhāva). Whoever worships Mātṛkā according to this very procedure [attains success]. 17.4.
He alone shall possess the divine nature, for he alone possesses the heroic state;
he who worships the Mātṛkā is truly wealthy and virtuous in this world. (17.5)
Śrī Mahādeva said:
O lady of excellent complexion, I shall now describe another general method:
having performed the previously mentioned meditation, one should recite the Mātṛkā-mantra. (17.6)
By the mere meditation on the letter *ka*, all accomplishments (*siddhi*) arise;
and by reciting the letter *ka*, O lady of beautiful limbs, one becomes beloved by all. (17.7)
Having recited all the Mātṛkās, or indeed the letter *ka* alone;
for the letter *ka* is the primordial nature (*mūlaprakṛti*) of all phonemes. (17.8)
Therefore, O Goddess, O Beloved, one should worship the letter *ka* with great effort;
the wise person should worship the Goddess every day, beginning with this first [letter]. (17.9)
Then one attains the fruit of them all and becomes composed of their essence; O auspicious lady, through the worship of the letter *ka*, there is the worship of them all. (17.10)
O lady of beautiful countenance, he who performs this every day or every month shall indeed become a divine hero and obtain the fruit of all worship.
O lady of tremulous glances, even if one does not perform [the worship] but merely remembers it in the mind,
he too shall always consist of all forms of worship and consist of all states of being.
Without knowing the reality of existence, how can one recite the mantra of Viṣṇu?
O Maheśānī, how could that vulgar person recite the mantra of Śakti? (17.13)
O Goddess, how can he recite the Śiva-mantra, the Saura-mantra, or the Gāṇeśa-mantra?
If one were to recite them ten million times without the knowledge of the essential nature (bhāvatattva), [it would be in vain]. 17.14
"O Goddess, all of that is in vain for him, and he shall fall into hell at every step.
O lady with tremulous eyes, how could such a man become a preceptor to divine heroes? (17.15)
O Goddess, O Beloved, he who is always like a beast is indeed a beast-like teacher;
being devoid of the reality of one's own nature, how could he perform the fifth sacrifice? (17.16)
But the Vaiṣṇava, O lady of beautiful hips, should worship the fifth syllable, *makāra*;
for it certainly becomes the body of the deity, O lady of beautiful hips. (17.17)
Thus I shall proclaim the mantra situated in the Ānanda-paṭala,
which consists of thirty syllables and is eternally the knowledge-mantra (vidyā) of Kālī, Chinnā, and the others.
Then that [practice] becomes filled with success; otherwise, it is always fruitless.
Therefore, having performed the meditation on the desired object, one should gaze into the center of the heart.
First, having meditated upon the beloved woman in full bloom, and immediately thereafter, by the mere meditation upon her in full bloom, the form of the deity arises. (17.20)
O Goddess, whichever one's chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) has blossomed forth,
one should meditate upon that beloved deity, O Goddess, by way of the visualization prescribed in the mantra.
The body of the deity certainly arises from the seed-syllable;
O Daughter of the Mountain, it is born from the first seed-syllable of the mantra. (17.22)
Those fifty Mātṛkās are all in the form of young women;
from that youthful body, indeed, the dark-complexioned form is born.
Rāma, whose eyes are like lotus petals, surely comes forth in full bloom;
from that seed, O Goddess, the supreme, eternal Brahman is born. (17.24)
Merely through the conjunction with the seed-syllable, the eternal Śabdabrahman [is attained].
I shall now proclaim another secret, singular and most wonderful. (17.25)

O Goddess, if one should recite [the mantra] ten million times without the fifty-fold convention of letters—the wonderful fifty principles which constitute the reality of the letters—[it is ineffective]. (17.26)
O Goddess, all that [is done] by him is in vain; he suffers loss at every step.
Within the twelve-petaled lotus of the heart, upon a golden throne, is the Beloved.

O Goddess, having meditated with effort upon the visualization of the letters within that womb—in the mandala in the center of the triangle—from the letter 'A' to the letter 'Kṣa'—[one should proceed]. (17.28)
O Goddess, one should meditate upon each [deity] individually within every group, both in direct and reverse order, within the womb-cage of the beloved.
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, having meditated with effort upon the letter *ka* of all the gods and goddesses, both in direct and reverse order, O Goddess. (17.30)
Indeed, the person who, having understood it, practices the convention of the fifty principles which consists of exactly fifty phonemes, the Vidyā quickly becomes propitious. (17.31)
O lady of beautiful hips, what is impossible for one to accomplish when the Vidyā is pleased with him?
O Supreme Goddess, the six cakras are the most excellent secret place.
O Dear One, that person who, having diligently meditated upon the lotus at the feet of the Guru within the thousand-spoked [mandala], performs the symbolic assignment of the fifty letters; 17.33.

O Goddess with tremulous glances, one shall now certainly bring Keśava under control by means of this secret; one shall also delude Rudra, who possesses the brilliance of the fire of universal destruction.
It would suddenly cause the entire universe, including all that moves and is immobile, to fall into delusion.
This, O Goddess, is the supreme method for the enchantment of the letters that I have described to you.
O Pārvatī, if one should mutter the mantra without knowing the delusive reality (mohana-tattva),
the worlds and the Gandharvas will indeed turn toward him with hostility.
O Goddess, this "Enchantment of the Letters" (varṇamohana), consisting of every single syllable, has been declared.
He who, without knowing the principle of enchantment, should attempt to enchant others [will fail]. (17.37)
O Goddess, all that [performed] for him is in vain; it shall never be otherwise.
Indeed, through the power of this reality, one shall attain perfection before long. (17.38)
One should recite the mantra within the womb [of the seed-syllable] in both forward and reverse order;
having recited it, one should bring even a single syllable back to its own place.
Again, O Goddess, having drawn forth the phoneme from the midst of the womb of the Kāminī,
one should mutter the syllable endowed with the lunar drop (candrabindu).
One should also meditate separately upon each of the fifty syllables;
O Goddess, he who recites this supreme mantra according to this procedure [attains success]. (17.41)
For him, success shall come quickly; otherwise, it will be fruitless.
O Goddess, it is written with such conviction that it becomes as if it were a literal syllable.
O lady of excellent hips, such recitation and worship are useless;
I shall now declare the special mantra that resides in the Chapter on Bliss (Ānandapaṭala). 17.43.
O Goddess, for one who knows and practices this mantra named Śrīmohana, which consists of fifty syllables, success is not far off. (17.44)
Otherwise, everything is fruitless; the secret is not fruitful at all.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the *Śrīkāmadhenu Tantra*, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The eighteenth chapter.
The venerable Mahādeva said:
Now I shall further proclaim another secret, most wonderful.
O lady of excellent complexion, a Vaiṣṇava who goes [elsewhere] without knowing this indeed goes to the Raurava hell.
O Goddess, he who thus recites the Supreme Sovereign joined with the principles (*tattva*),
when he recites this Vidyā consisting of nine principles, O Pārvatī— (18.2)
At that very moment, O beautiful goddess, success arises suddenly for one who, having understood the mantra consisting of nine principles, recites it even once. (18.3)
At that very moment, O Goddess, he will certainly become equal to Viṣṇu;
first, O lotus-eyed one, one should meditate upon the beloved woman within the lotus of the heart.
The wise one should first utter the seed-syllable, and immediately after that, the Kāminī; then, with effort, he should again utter the second seed-syllable. (18.5)
Then, having meditated upon the beloved woman, one should utter the third seed-syllable.
By this method, O Goddess, there is the encapsulation by the meditation on the beloved woman.
Furthermore, O Pārvatī, perform the meditation on the letter *ka* in direct order (*anuloma*); O Goddess, perform it in reverse order (*viloma*) in the same manner as the direct order. (18.7)
In this manner, O Goddess of gods, O beloved, by diligently practicing each syllable in sequence, O lady of excellent hips, one shall become a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis).
Having meditated again and again on each of all the syllables of the mantra individually,
and having meditated on Kāminī at the beginning and the end, one becomes composed of Śiva and Śakti.

Or else, O lady with tremulous eyes and lotus-like face, O beloved, one should recite the mantra after placing the seed-syllable at the beginning, in the middle, and likewise at the end, within the heart-lotus.
At that very moment, O Goddess, a divine form suddenly arises;
yet in the Kali age in Bhārata, the mantra is always overcome by sleep.
O lady of beautiful limbs, by this secret [mantra], the breaking of sleep shall then occur.
O lady of excellent hips, one should first recite it three times in the direct order.
Having meditated and recited [the mantra] three times in reverse order within the lotus of the heart, I shall now explain another matter: the characteristics of the interruption of sleep.
O Pārvatī, having first meditated upon the beloved woman and then immediately thereafter,
one should recite the mantra ten times for the purpose of breaking her sleep.
Then, O Goddess of beautiful limbs, one should mutter this secret mantra which causes the entire universe to bloom and delude; by this, the form of Viṣṇu arises.

O Dear One, [one should meditate upon] the God who bears the conch and the discus, whose essence is the pure reality, who wears yellow garments, who is peaceful, and whose lotus-face is serene. (18.16)
With arms reaching down to his knees, adorned with a forest garland, his form graced by the three-fold bend (tribhaṅga), and beautified by a lovely crest-jewel. || 18.17 ||
The form of Viṣṇu arises, resplendent with the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem;
it is Kṛṣṇa himself in his incarnation, smooth as delicate collyrium.
Or else, O Goddess of pure smiles, Hari—who abides in the midst of the circle of gopīs and consists of manifold pleasures—is born from that seed. (18.19)
By the mere meditation upon the beloved woman, the deity is certainly born;
this secret, O lady of beautiful limbs, should be held within the center of the heart. (18.20)
This is, without doubt, the essence of all secrets;
now I shall proclaim another secret that is most wonderful.
O Daughter of the Mountain, having first meditated upon a passionate woman in the center of one's heart,
one should mentally contemplate the mantra within her womb.
O beautiful one, one should meditate upon the deity within that womb by means of the path of visualization;
then, having visualized the beloved once more, Hari shall manifest from her.
O Goddess, "Hari" is an illustration; indeed, [the name] of all [deities] has been fashioned [in this way].
O Maheśānī, the mantra of the Vidyā should always be accompanied by the word for sleep (nidrā). 18.24.
Therefore, O auspicious lady, if one should recite [the mantra] even once while free from sleep, one certainly and suddenly obtains ten million times the merit from that recitation. (18.25)
O fair-complexioned one, when the left arm trembles, then Manu is afflicted by sleep;
and when the right arm trembles, [the same occurs]. (18.26)
At that very moment, O lady of tremulous glances, Manu is forever awakened;
for this reason, O beautiful one, the wise man should perform his recitation while remaining awake. (18.27)
The Goddess said:
O Mahādeva, if at the time of worship one should become overcome by sleep, how then can the mantra be perfected? What should be done then, O Lord? (18.28)
"By what rite should one recite [the mantra], or should one not recite it? Tell me, O Lord!
Śrī Mahādeva said: "I shall declare the secret mantra that resides in the Ānandapaṭala. (18.29)
O lady of beautiful limbs, this twelve-syllable mantra, which illuminates the breaking of sleep,
will be fruitless if one does not know this secret mantra.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The nineteenth chapter.
Śrī Mahādeva said: O lady of pure smiles, no doubt whatsoever should be entertained at the time of worship.
Having suddenly meditated upon the beloved woman, one should utter the Turīyakūṭa.
At that very moment, O Goddess, Manu shall suddenly be freed from sleep;
he should then mutter the mantra ten times, O Goddess, either mentally within his heart or even with his speech.
O Maheśānī, O lady of excellent complexion, if one should abandon the *dakṣiṇā* at the time of worship, there must be an expiation for that mantra.
O Goddess, if one performs this expiation and recites the mantra, what is the use of his right arm? What is the use of one who is afflicted by sleep? (19.4)
O lady of beautiful limbs, this secret mantra is the definitive [instruction] for the time of worship;
O lady of beautiful limbs, this secret is auspicious during all states of sleep.
O lady of beautiful limbs, when the wind flows through the left arm and when it flows through the right,
having kept this secret, one should recite the mantra.
At that very moment, she abandoned her sleep; the Vidyā and the Mantra were no longer otherwise.
The Vidyā consisted of Yoganidrā, and the Mantra consisted of Yoganidrā.
I shall declare the special mantra situated in the Ānanda-paṭala: the eight-syllabled Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), which is an illuminator and the very form of liberation. (19.8)
Becoming composed of all accomplishments, one shall obtain the fruit of the secret;
if one recites [the mantra] even while asleep, what need is there for his recitation and worship?
O lady of beautiful limbs, by this secret [mantra], eternal sleep is abandoned;
she who is of the nature of Brahman abides within the central path of the *suṣumṇā*. (19.10)
O fair-limbed one, listen attentively as I describe the sin of him who recites a mantra without knowing this secret. (19.11)
O Goddess, whatever chapter written by a Śūdra is recited, the man who does so attains each and every hell. (19.12)
Indeed, within the thirty-two crores of hells,
those lowest of men are cooked in succession, having been taken up by crores of bamboo rods.
O Daughter of the Mountain, O Beloved, whether he be a Brahmin, a Kshatriya, or even a Vaishya, they are cooked in a terrible hell for causing a Shudra to transcribe [the scripture]. (19.14)
Therefore, a wise person should not recite a chapter written by a Śūdra.
Hence, O Goddess, one must perform the essential meditation on the Kāminī.
Then, O Goddess, one becomes perfected through the Vidyā-mantra and not otherwise;
merely by meditating upon the beloved woman, one shall become possessed of all perfections.
The goal would be accomplished by this alone; why do you worship with so many?
Out of devotion for you, I have declared that which is to be kept secret throughout the three worlds.
If one performs worship after knowing this [mantra] to be the wish-fulfilling cow (kāmadhenu), that worship shall become fruitful and the recitation (japa) shall always be successful. (19.18)
Otherwise, initiation is like that of a ghost, and worship is always like that of a ghost.
Having first meditated upon the beloved woman, one should perform the recitation and worship. (19.19)
Having obtained the fruit of the wish-fulfilling cow, one becomes identical with Sadāśiva;
he himself would be the form of Viṣṇu, for he is indeed Mahāmāyā herself.
O lady of pure smiles, honored by the gods, this mantra known as Kāmadhenu is highly praised within the Śiva-mantra, the Viṣṇu-mantra, and the Śakti-mantra. (19.21)
O Goddess, this which is the essence of essences, higher than the highest, has been told to you;
by performing which the practitioner goes to the abode of liberation, so difficult to attain. (19.22)
I shall now declare the special mantra, the Vidyā whose form is the glorious Kāmarūpa;
without knowing this, meditation upon the Kāminī will suddenly become fruitless. (19.23)
O lady of tremulous glances, that meditation resides within the layer of bliss;
therefore, one must certainly and constantly recite this mantra which illuminates desire. (19.24)
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The twentieth chapter.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O you who are worshipped by the gods, please tell me the reality of the offering of the mantra."
To whom should one entrust the mantra? Tell me, O Ancient God.
O Lord of Devas, if the wielder of the trident should withdraw the splendors of the mantras, then, O God, the practitioner would instantly become devoid of luster. (20.2)
"What is the use of chanting, what is the use of worship, and furthermore, what is the use of preparatory rites?
O illustrious one, O Supreme Lord, please tell me that out of compassion. (20.3)
The illustrious Mahādeva said: "Well asked by you, O blessed lady; now I shall tell you.
Having recited [the mantra], O lady of tremulous glances, one should meditate upon the Supreme Beloved. (20.4)

O lady of excellent hips, having joined each syllable of the mantra with the moon-bindu (the nasal dot) within the cave of the passionate woman's elephant, one should recite it ten times for each individual syllable.
O Goddess, perform it in reverse just as you did in direct order.
Beyond this, O lady of excellent hips, having recognized the supreme woman of desire (kāminī), [proceed].
O Maheśānī, one should recite the mantra *viyat-brahma-kāminī* ten times;
O Dear One, the syllable *viyat* joined with *vahni* should be placed within the womb of *kāminī*.
One should recite the seed-syllable with devotion ten times;
then, having meditated upon the principle of the beloved (kāminī-tattva) on the forehead, it shall indeed become so.
And in this way, O Dear One, one should meditate upon the beloved woman in the place of the Mātṛkās;
one should recite the Mātṛkā-mantra in the fifty places of the Mātṛkās.
O Goddess, quickly transform the seed-syllable into a passionate woman amidst the clusters of light;
O Goddess, one should recite this supreme seed-syllable of the passionate woman ten times.
Perform the recitation within the womb of the beloved, in the principle of light (jyotis-tattva).
O lady of excellent hips, the principle of light is itself the eternal life-force (jīva).
Having established the vital principle (tattva) of the beloved woman, the wise practitioner,
having placed that supreme beloved within the great thousand-petaled lotus (sahasrāra), [should proceed].
With the mantra "O you who guard the secret beyond secrets," the knower of mantras should offer the external worship and other offerings into the right hand of the deity.
O lady of beautiful hips, by offering [the mantra] into the left hand of the Goddess, one becomes a partaker of the fruit;
for, O beloved, all the splendors of the recitation reside in the hand of the Goddess.
Having offered [it], O Supreme Goddess, the practitioner becomes one with that splendor;
what need has he for worship, O Auspicious One, and what need for recitation, O Fair-faced One? (20.15)
O Goddess, whatever is given, all of it dissolves into Brahman;
O Goddess, one should mutter the mantra of knowledge, and its splendor arises.
O Goddess with tremulous glances, one should never offer [the substance] into the hand of a deity without the principle of life (jīvatattva), and especially not into the hand of the Goddess.
Therefore, O Goddess, you must certainly establish the principle of life (jīvatattva) with great effort;
for if one were to offer the deity without the principle of life, O Goddess, [the offering would be fruitless].
O Goddess, if one performs recitation, it becomes fruitless, and the worship also becomes fruitless;
whatever there may be, such as perfumes, flowers, and so forth, one should offer all of that to the God.
O lady of excellent hips, the reality of recitation (japa-tattva) is always composed of all splendor;
O lady of excellent hips, if one were to offer that splendor to the Goddess or to the God, [it would be so].
How can accomplishment arise for one whose vital breath is constantly [absorbed into] the fire? O Goddess, O Beloved, he who offers his vital energy [into the fire] shall return again. (20/21)
O lady of tremulous glances, that splendor is difficult for the practitioner to attain;
O beautiful woman, a base man creates fear in vain.
If one should recite even ten million times without knowing the dedication (*samarpaṇa*),
O Dear One, one shall enter into the splendor of that deity amidst the deity's own brilliance.
One should meditate with great effort, as if it were a casket containing all one's possessions.
O Goddess, this principle of life, which is very difficult to attain, has been explained to you. (20.24)

By performing which the practitioner attains the rare form of Brahman—having heard this tantra, O Goddess, one shall obtain the fruit of the secret. O beloved of excellent gait, the practitioner should listen to this tantra. (20.25)
Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the *Kāmadhenu Tantra*, in the dialogue between the God and the Goddess.
The twenty-first chapter.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
"If one should recite [the mantra] over a passionate woman during an eclipse of the moon or the sun,"
At that very moment, accomplishment arises suddenly; there is no doubt about this. || 21/1 ||
If, having first recited the Kāminī mantra, one should then recite one's own vidyās, and thereafter recite the Kāminī again, one will become a master of all siddhis. || 21.2 ||
O beloved, one should not recite [the mantra] during an eclipse without knowing the true nature of the woman;
O auspicious lady, if a person of deluded intellect recites during an eclipse out of ignorance, [he incurs a fault]. (21.3)
O Goddess, all of that for him is in vain, and his prior merit perishes;
the lunar festival and the solar festival are never to be disregarded. (21.4)
O lady of beautiful hips, if a base person does not witness the solar festival, let alone the higher dharma, even the prior dharma perishes. (21.5)
If one does not see [the truth] due to ignorance, one shall encounter every misfortune;
such a person is always filled with all misfortunes and filled with all sins.
Therefore, O Goddess, one must certainly observe the lunar eclipse;
likewise, by observing the solar eclipse, one shall attain liberation.

O beloved with tremulous glances, if a foolish-souled man, without knowing the calculation of the zodiac signs and so forth, fails to observe an eclipse even after due consideration, [he incurs sin]. (21.8)
The merit previously acquired perishes at that very moment;
therefore, one should observe an eclipse of the moon or sun with great care.
O blessed lady, what need has he for a woman, and again, what need for beautiful things?
Having recited [the mantra] from the first morsel of food until liberation, one becomes a master of supernatural powers (siddhīśvara). (21.10)
O lady of beautiful limbs, if one does not recite [the mantra], one shall go to the Raurava hell;
at that time, O lady of tremulous glances, you are the very embodiment of the Supreme Brahman.
At that time, O lady of excellent limbs, from the distinction of castes such as the Kṣatriyas down to the Cāṇḍālas and others, all indeed become equal to the twice-born.
O lady with tremulous eyes, the twice-born are indeed Brahman itself; of this there is no doubt.
O goddess of beautiful countenance, what need is there to mention the Cāṇḍālas in that regard? (21.13)
Therefore, one should diligently perform the observation of the lunar eclipse;
O Goddess, it is ten million times more meritorious than [the solar], and the solar [eclipse] is ten times [more meritorious than that]. (21.14)
In that regard, O beloved goddess, whatever action is performed there—such as recitation, fire-offerings, and so forth—that shall become inexhaustible; this is my certain word. (21.15)

If one observes [the planets] according to the Yavanas, having abandoned the calculation starting from the zodiac signs (rāśi) and so forth, then for the Yavana, success is thus achieved upon the surface of the earth. (21.16)
Whether one is initiated or uninitiated, upon seeing [the deity], one should perform a bath;
thus, O beloved, this imperishable bath becomes equivalent to a bath in the Gaṅgā. (21.17)
Water situated even in a pit of excrement is considered equal to the water of the Gaṅgā;
it is praised at the time of an eclipse, but not otherwise—this is my word. (21.18)
O lady of excellent complexion, if a child should be more than six months old, a bath during an eclipse of the moon or the sun is recommended for him. (21.19)
Without performing bathing and giving gifts, he would suddenly go to hell;
he is fallen, he is most sinful, and he will suddenly become a pig, O beloved. (21.20)
O Goddess, O Beloved, her food and water become urine and blood;
of this there is no doubt, such is my word, O fair-faced one. (21.21)
O Pārvatī, on the occasion of a lunar eclipse, whether one be a Brāhmaṇa or a non-Brāhmaṇa—
even everyone from a Cāṇḍāla onwards— proceeds as belonging to the lineage of Brahmā.
Why should one calculate the sum of all things by the name "Brahman"?
Therefore, O lady of tremulous glances, one should never form such a conceptualization. (21.23)
O Pārvatī, O lady of excellent hips, one need not consider the months, fortnights, lunar days, or other astrological signs during an eclipse of the moon or the sun.
But at the time of the release of the morsel [of breath] and so forth, where is the month? Where is the lunar day?
That time is the Supreme Brahman, visible to the eyes of all. (21.25)
Therefore, O beloved, how could the ignorant world, having abandoned the eclipse, consider anything else when it comes to the calculation of the lunar mansions and so forth? (21.26)
By the inference of Brahmā, he would be submerged in Raurava;
having returned from Raurava, he proceeds again into a sinful womb.
O lady of beautiful limbs, there is never any atonement for that either;
therefore, one should abandon everything and gaze upon the moon during the parvan.
O Goddess, as it is on the lunar festival day, so it is on the solar festival day, O Beloved;
having abandoned the performance of śrāddha and other such rites there, one should recite the vidyā-mantra, O Dear One. (21.29)
Otherwise, one goes to hell and leads seven generations of ancestors downward.
O beautiful one, listen as I shall declare another secret.
One should visualize [the letters] from *a* to *kṣa* within each individual lotus;
thereafter, one should recite the syllable *śūnya* (the letter *ha*) conjoined with the moon-bindu (*i*).
Then, in the empty space of the heart and within the luminous spheres,
the wise one should recite the Mātṛkā in both direct and reverse order.
Then, O Goddess, the best of practitioners should manifest the seed-syllable of the letters (varṇabīja) upon the cowrie shell, like the seed of a lotus, as the Mātṛkā.
Having encased the seed-syllable of the Moon, one of clear intellect should recite the letter;
by reciting it both in direct and reverse order, one becomes composed of nectar.
O lotus-eyed one, having meditated solely upon the beloved with a face full of blossoming joy, the deity or the goddess arises from the seed-syllable; then,
having meditated upon the deity and beheld the divine form, [one should proceed].
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra, in the dialogue between Mahādeva and Mahādevī.

The twenty-fourth chapter:
Śrī Mahādeva said:
O Lord of Yogins, O treasury of compassion, please tell me the secret of the rosary (mālārahasya);
for if one recites the mantra from the tail [end], it would take away the splendors of its face.
If one recites the mantra from the mouth while the tail is flickering, O lady of beautiful limbs, that recitation becomes fruitless when the tail is flickering. (23.2)
The venerable Lord said: O Goddess, the fifty-syllable [mantra] is strung upon the variegated channels;
having established the syllables in the east, Sumeru is indeed the tail and the satiating one.
Having served Sumeru and [offered] the *akarādi* and so forth, one should recite [the mantra], O lady of beautiful limbs;
for the secret of the rosary is to be well-guarded throughout the three worlds. (23.4)
O beloved, just as the distinction between castes and the distinction between individual souls are well-concealed, I shall proclaim the mantra of the living soul; listen attentively.
The conclusion is that the mantra of the individual soul (jīva-mantra) and the mantra of the caste (jāti-mantra) are equal;
O Maheśānī, just as meditation becomes equal in its effect upon living.
Listen to that meditation, O lady of beautiful limbs, and attend to it with careful attention: [She is] two-armed, with a body as fair as gold, and clothed in yellow silk garments. (23.7)
Her limbs were radiant with various ornaments; she was a young maiden in the bloom of fresh youth, her body anointed with black fragrant unguents, and she took her seat upon the throne of the Sun.
Her fingers were slender and long, resplendent with moon-like nails;
she was adorned with two breasts shaped like *kadamba* buds. || 23.9 ||
Her mouth was filled with betel-leaf mixed with a portion of camphor,
and she was adorned with eyebrows graced by hundreds of thousands of sidelong glances.
O Great Goddess, [one should meditate on her] illuminated by a vermilion tilaka and adorned with curved locks of hair;
in this way, O Maheśānī, the life-force always remains present everywhere. (23.11)
O beloved, I have thus explained to you all of this— the doctrine of the Kāmadhenu— as it resides within the Chapter on Bliss for all beings, beginning with the twice-born.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the dialogue between the Goddess and the Lord within the Śrī Kāmadhenu Tantra.
This Kāmadhenu Tantra is completed.
